EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
RE Number | RE-WA-2021-0077
Application Type | Renewal
Date of Record | 4 April 2025
Commodity | Wheat
Destination | Vietnam
ABN | 25 678 901 237
1. Establishment Details
Business Name | Goldfields Grain Storage Pty Ltd
Trading Name | Goldfields Grain Storage Pty Ltd
Address | Lot 5 Goldfields Highway, Kalgoorlie WA 6430
State/Territory | WA
Contact Person | Glen Nakamura
Business Structure | Proprietary company
Registration Number | RE-WA-2021-0077
Registration Expiry | 5 June 2024
2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for wheat (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Wheat receival | Intake of bulk and bagged wheat from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of wheat to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of wheat in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-WA-2021-0077 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 6 June 2021 and the current registration period extends to 5 June 2024. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Glen Nakamura is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2017. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises are located at Lot 5 Goldfields Highway, Kalgoorlie WA 6430. The establishment occupies the main farm site including storage sheds and associated infrastructure. The site is bounded by the main road to the north and farm fencing on remaining sides.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: wheat is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of wheat. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for Vietnam:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required; MARD additional import conditions apply
Fumigation | Phosphine treatment documented; records held for ≥2 years
Residue Compliance | Comply with Vietnam Ministry of Health MRL tables
12. Supporting Documents
Farm Site Plan (Appendix A)
HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

I acknowledge the obligations under the Export Control Act 2020 and the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

Establishment: Coffs Harbour Produce Pty Ltd
Address: 27 Station Road, Tasmania

Scope: Receival, storage, cleaning and bulk loading of canola and linseed for export. Cold pressing of linseed oil (in-line). Registered area RE-WA-1882, Kwinana facility.
Intended use: Canola for crushing/oil extraction. Linseed oil for food and industrial use. Destination: Japan (canola), Germany (linseed oil). Non-GM canola for EU markets.

Operator 27A

3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Paddock planning & variety selection | Variety/agronomy plans | Seed selection — GM-status documented
2 | Harvest & field transport | Standing crop | Harvested oilseed at receival pit
3 | Receival / intake testing | Bulk oilseed | Oil content, moisture, impurities tested at intake
4 | Drying / conditioning | Wet grain (>9% moisture) | Dried oilseed ≤8% moisture
5 | Storage | Dry oilseed | Stored in designated silo — GM and non-GM segregated
6 | Cleaning / scalping | Stored oilseed | Cleaned of trash, weed seeds and foreign material
7 | Cold pressing (linseed only) | Clean linseed | Linseed oil extracted; meal collected
8 | Bulk loading (canola) | Cleaned canola | Loaded to bulk vessel via pneumatic conveyor
9 | Tanker filling (linseed oil) | Pressed linseed oil | Filled to food-grade tanker
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1–2 | Chem | Glucosinolates above export spec (canola) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
1–2 | Chem | Erucic acid above EU limit (0.5%) — old varieties | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
1 | Chem | Pesticide MRL exceedance — herbicide, fungicide | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
3–5 | Chem | Mycotoxin (Ochratoxin A, aflatoxin) from wet/damaged seed | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
5 | Bio | Insect infestation (grain weevils, beetles) in storage | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Bio | Rodent infestation in silos | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
6 | Phys | Foreign material — stones, steel, glass | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
7 | Chem | PAH contamination from pressing equipment (lubricants) | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
8–9 | Phys | Transport unit/tanker contamination (previous cargo) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Chem | GM cross-contamination of non-GM lots (Identity Preservation) | 3 | 3 | 9 | CCP-5 | See HACCP Control Chart
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; residue test on flag lots | MRL per Japan / EU Regulation 396/2005 | Spray records checked each grower per harvest; residue test 5% of receival lots | Per grower/season | Reject lot; quarantine; grower notified; DAFF notified | QA Manager
CCP-2 | Storage | Mycotoxin | Moisture monitoring; aeration; temperature probe | OA ≤3 µg/kg; aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg | Intake moisture test; monthly temperature probe; lab test on export lots | Monthly during storage; per export consignment | Segregate affected silo; test; downgrade or destroy if above threshold | QA Manager
CCP-3 | Storage | Rodent infestation | 16 perimeter bait stations; monthly inspection | No visible live rodents or fresh signs in storage zone | Monthly bait station inspection (Form AOW-PC-01); pitfall traps quarterly | Monthly | Engage licensed contractor immediately; quarantine affected silo | Plant Manager
CCP-4 | Cleaning/Scalping | Foreign material | Scalper (6 mm screen), rare-earth magnetic separator | No metal > 2 mm; no glass; no hard foreign matter | Scalper screen inspection each shift; magnet cleaning log | Each shift | Stop line; remove contaminant; inspect product; re-screen | Plant Manager
CCP-5 | Storage/Loading | GM cross-contamination | Dedicated IP silos for non-GM; flush/cleanout procedures; GM test on non-GM lots | <0.9% adventitious GM presence (EU threshold) | PCR test on non-GM lots at receival and pre-shipment | Per non-GM lot | Reject non-GM classification; re-test; notify customer | QA Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No site-specific hygiene and sanitation program documented for Coffs Harbour Produce Pty Ltd. General industry practices are referenced but no cleaning schedules, chemicals, personnel hygiene procedures or records are defined.
Waste Management Procedure (AOW-WMP-001):
• Scalper screenings / trash: collected in sealed bins; transported off-site to approved composting.
• Oilseed dust: cyclone dust collector; dust collected in sealed bags; removed weekly.
• Linseed meal (pressing by-product): sold to livestock feed market; removed within 48 hours of pressing.
• Chemical waste: fumigant and pesticide containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
• Wastewater from cleaning: directed to grease trap; collected by liquid waste contractor monthly.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal pest control program is documented for Coffs Harbour Produce Pty Ltd. No bait station map, monitoring schedule, contractor engagement or corrective action procedures are included.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
Traceability System (AOW-TRACE-001):
• Each silo assigned unique ID (silo number + commodity + IP/non-GM status + season).
• Receival dockets link grower → farm block → variety → quantity → silo.
• Dispatch: bill of lading links silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination.
• GM testing records linked to lot reference; retained 5 years (EU requirement).
• One-step-forward / one-step-back trace exercise performed semi-annually.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
Failed Goods Procedure (AOW-FGP-001):
• GM contamination above threshold: lot re-classified as non-Identity Preserved; customer notified; DAFF notified.
• Mycotoxin exceedance: silo placed on HOLD; re-test from secondary sample; if confirmed, dispose to non-food use.
• Pesticide MRL: reject export consignment; segregate; grower liability documented; option to process to domestic oil (if MRL met under FSANZ).
• All non-conformances recorded in AOW-NCR register with root cause analysis.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Coffs Harbour Produce Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
Establishment Name | Goldfields Grain Storage
RE Number | RE-WA-2021-0077
State / Territory | WA
Property Address | Lot 5 Goldfields Highway, Kalgoorlie WA 6430
Registered Commodity | Specialty Grains
Responsible Officer | Donna Fielding
Property Area | 85.0 ha
Year Established | 2021
Document Version | 2.0
Plan Date | 1 July 2024
Next Review | 1 July 2026
1.  OVERVIEW
Goldfields Grain Storage is a registered export establishment located at Lot 5 Goldfields Highway, Kalgoorlie WA 6430, WA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-WA-2021-0077 and is registered to handle and export Specialty Grains under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
RB | Receival & Processing Building | 40×25 m | Steel/concrete | Centre of site
S1–S6 | Storage Bins | Dia. 12 m | Galv. steel | South cluster
PL | Packing & Dispatch Shed | 35×20 m | Tilt-up concrete | SE corner
AM | Amenities Block | 9×5 m | Brick | Adjacent RB
CH | Chemical Store | 6×4 m | Steel, bunded | NW corner
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 6×5 m | Enclosed room | RB north end
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Receival pit and elevator | 1 unit | Primary receival
Cleaning and separation unit | 1 unit | Pre-storage cleaning
Drying system | batch | Moisture reduction
Packing/bagging line | 1 unit | Export preparation
Weighing system | In-line | Lot verification
In-line quality sampler | 1 unit | Representative sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Specialty Grains.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 470 lux packing hall, 360 lux cool store entry, 342 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
The main processing building was constructed in 2021 using rough-sawn pine wall framing and cladding. The internal surface is porous and heavily textured — pressure washing disperses rather than removes accumulated dust and product residue from the grain of the timber. Floor surfaces are unsealed concrete (original 2021 pour) with surface crazing and crack networks retaining product debris. No coved skirting at floor-wall junctions.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-135, version 2.0, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Product waste and screenings | Collection hoppers under cleaning unit | Daily removal
Grain dust | Bag filter or cyclone | Fortnightly
Washdown water | Drains → contained sump | Weekly
Packaging waste | Covered skip | Fortnightly contractor
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 8 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: March 2025).
8.  SERVICES
Service | Details
Electrical supply | Three-phase 415 V — Western Power connection at site entry
Water supply | self-supplied bore — 32 mm service
Telecommunications | NBN fixed line + mobile backup at administration/control room
Sewerage | Septic system — licensed — serves amenities block
Stormwater | Sheet flow to soakage trench with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 60 kVA generator — auto-start on grid failure

Position | Establishment Manager
Date | 1 July 2024
Signature |

2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Goldfields Grain Storage used in pulse cleaning, storage and packing operations for export Lupins. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Lupins during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Una Chambers | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Hopper | After each intake | Remove pulse residue from hopper, conveyor, and floor. Blow out crevices with compressed air. | Dry / compressed air | Receival Staff | Intake checklist
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter | After each run | Remove screenings. Brush screens and rollers. Inspect for blockages. | Dry method | Plant Operator | Run log
Storage Silos / Bins | Between lots | Full sweep-out of walls, cone, and floor. Inspect for residue and insect activity. | Dry sweep | Storage Manager | Pre-loading checklist
Packing Line / Bagging Machine | End of each shift | Clear product residue. Wipe conveyor, scales, and packing tables. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Operator | Shift log
Palletising Area / Loading Dock | After each dispatch | Remove packaging debris. Sweep dock floor. Check for spills. | Dry sweep + spot clean | Dispatch Staff | Dispatch record
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, floors, basins, toilets. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Hopper
After each intake run: Lock out receiving conveyor. Use compressed air lance to dislodge pulse residue from hopper walls, conveyor trough, and all transition points. Vacuum accumulated screenings and fine material. Inspect underside of conveyor belt for product trapping. Record in Intake Checklist.
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter
After each cleaning run: Remove accumulated screenings from collection trays and hoppers. Brush aspirator screens with dedicated brush to remove lodged seeds. For colour sorter: follow manufacturer's lens cleaning protocol. Vacuum sensor housings. Inspect all filters and replace if blocked. Record in Plant Operator Run Log.
Storage Silos / Bins
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Storage Silos / Bins in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Packing Line / Bagging Machine
End of each shift: Clear all pulse product from the line. Vacuum or brush conveyor belts, weigh hoppers, and bag former guides to remove pulse fines. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe external surfaces of bagging machine and packing bench. Check sealing jaws and heat elements for residue. Record in Shift Log.
Palletising Area / Loading Dock
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Palletising Area / Loading Dock in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Dead-stock accumulation occurs in aspirator collection trays, conveyor trough joints, and under the bagging machine floor plate. These areas are vacuumed or blown out at each run change to prevent insect harbourage.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | Floors, packing area | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Amenities, hand-contact surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
AcidRinse 500 Descaler | AgriChem Aust | Acidic cleaner | 1:50 in water | Scale mineral deposits | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Cleaning records are maintained in the site office. The establishment retains completed records for a period of six months after the end of the relevant activity.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
The establishment manager or nominated supervisor conducts a visual inspection of all cleaned areas prior to production commencement. Any deficiency identified is corrected before the area is cleared for use.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Goldfields Grain Storage (conducted 14 July 2025) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.

CCP-1 | Receival/Storage | Mycotoxin | Intake moisture test; aeration; temperature probe; lab test on export lots | Aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg; OA ≤3 µg/kg | Moisture probe each lot; monthly temp probe; NATA test on flag lots | Monthly; per export consignment | Segregate; re-test; downgrade to feed if confirmed | Operations Manager
CCP-2 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; residue test on 5% of lots | MRL per India, Pakistan, Bangladesh (CODEX/strictest) | Spray records each grower; residue test flagged lots | Per grower/season | Quarantine; reject; notify grower; DAFF notification | Operations Manager
CCP-3 | Pre-cleaning/Sizing | Foreign material | Pre-cleaner + gravity table + optical sorter + metal detector | No metal >2 mm; no stones; no glass | Metal detector calibrated each shift; visual inspection each lot | Each shift | Stop line; remove contaminant; inspect; re-run | Operations Manager
CCP-4 | Fumigation | Phosphine residue | Licensed fumigator; ventilation protocol; residue test | ≤0.01 mg/kg at load-out | Licensed fumigator certificate; vent period checklist | Each fumigation event | Extend vent; re-test; do not load until cleared | Operations Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (DDPE-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of receival pit, conveyors, pre-cleaner, gravity table, colour sorter and packing lines.
• During season: colour sorter air nozzles cleaned daily; packing tables sanitised between shifts.
• Personnel: handwash on entry; no food in processing area; dust masks and gloves provided.
• Records: Cleaning Register (DDPE-CLN-01) signed after each event.
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Orange District Fruit Co-operative Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (DDPE-PCP-001):
• Rodents: 14 perimeter bait stations; monthly inspection; licensed contractor quarterly.
• Insects: pitfall traps in sealed shed; phosphine fumigation when insects detected.
• Bird exclusion: netting at loading bay; doors kept closed.
• Records: Pest Control Log (DDPE-PC-01) monthly.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
This HACCP plan does not include a documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch.

Specifically absent:
• No lot coding system for receival batches.
• No documented one-step-back / one-step-forward traceability procedure.
• No dispatch register linking packed bags to container and destination.
• No recall procedure or trace exercise schedule.

ACTION REQUIRED: Implement a Traceability System covering:
(a) Unique lot codes at receival; (b) Processing batch records; (c) Packing lot codes on bags;
(d) Dispatch register; (e) Annual trace exercise; (f) Recall activation protocol; (g) Record retention minimum 2 years.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.
Failed Goods Procedure (DDPE-FGP-001):
• Mycotoxin exceedance: lot placed on HOLD; re-test; if confirmed — downgrade to feed or destroy.
• Pesticide MRL failure: quarantine; reject export; notify grower; DAFF notified.
• Foreign material detection: stop line; remove contaminant; inspect batch; re-run.
• Non-conformance records maintained in DDPE-NCR register.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Orange District Fruit Co-operative Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

1.  OVERVIEW
Condamine Valley Grain Co-operative is a registered export establishment located at 44 Cunningham Highway, Millmerran QLD 4357, QLD. The establishment holds RE Number RE-QLD-2022-0077 and is registered to handle and export Apples under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
PH | Packing Hall | 35×22 m | Tilt-up concrete, epoxy floor | Centre of site

CH | Chemical Store | 5×4 m | Steel, bunded slab | SW corner
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 6×5 m | Enclosed steel room in PH | PH north wall
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Fruit washing and brushing line | 1 unit | Pre-grading hygiene
Optical grader (weight/colour/defect) | 1 unit | Export grade sorting
Sticker/label applicator | 1 unit | Retail and export labelling
Palletiser | 1 unit | Export pallet build
Weigh-price labeller | 1 unit | Consumer pack verification
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Apples.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 500 lux processing, 400 lux storage, 380 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (1500 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1001 Rev 3): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Fruit culls and trim waste | Bins at grading line, hourly removal to compost bay | Daily
Washdown water | Recessed drains → grease trap → trade waste | Weekly grease trap inspection
Packaging waste (film, cardboard, foam) | Baler in external waste bay | Fortnightly collection
Chemical containers | Sealed store, labelled | Quarterly licensed disposal
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated apples residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1.  ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
Establishment Name | Condamine Valley Grain Co-operative
RE Number | RE-QLD-2022-0077
State / Territory | QLD
Property Address | 44 Cunningham Highway, Millmerran QLD 4357
Registered Commodity | Walnuts
Operation Type | Nut
Responsible Officer | Donna Fielding
Property Area | 265.0 ha

Plan Date | 29 June 2025
Next Review | 29 June 2027
Policy Context | Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021 / DAFF IMLS-12-3742 Element 3
2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers the receival, processing and packing areas of the establishment. Cold storage and grain silo hygiene are managed as part of routine maintenance schedules.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Walnuts during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Donna Fielding | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Area | After each intake | Remove nut debris, hulls, shells. Sweep floor and conveyor. Clear pit. | Dry sweep | Receival Staff | Intake record
Huller / Cracker / Sheller | After each run | Dismantle screens and access panels. Remove residue. Wipe rollers and blades. | BioDegreaser FD (1:25) + rinse | Processing Operator | Equipment cleaning log
Grading & Sizing Equipment | After each run | Clear product from screens. Brush surfaces. Wipe down conveyor belts and rollers. | EnzymeClear (1:20) | Grading Operator | Run record
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer | After each drying cycle | Remove nut skins and debris. Clean dryer mesh or tray surfaces. | Dry method | Drying Supervisor | Drying log
Packing Line / Packaging Area | End of each shift | Remove nut fragments from conveyor, scales, packing tables. Sweep floor. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, basins, toilets, floors. Refill soap. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Area
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Huller / Cracker / Sheller
After each production run: Power off and lock out drive before opening. Dismantle outer access panels. Remove nut residue, shell fragments, and skin from rollers, screens, and internal surfaces using a stiff brush. Prepare BioDegreaser FD at 1:25. Apply to metal surfaces where oil residue is present. Contact time 5 minutes. Rinse with water. Allow to dry before reassembly. Record in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Grading & Sizing Equipment
After each run: Clear all nut product from grading screens and conveyor belts. Brush screens using designated nut-cleaning brush to remove embedded skins and fragments. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20 in a spray bottle. Spray conveyor belt and rollers. Wipe with clean cloth. Inspect for any remaining organic residue. Record in Run Record.
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Drying Area / Pads / Dryer in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Storage Bins / Holding Area
Between commodity lots: Inspect and clean storage bins before loading a new nut commodity. Using industrial vacuum, remove all residual nut material from bin walls, seams, and floor. Inspect for pest activity (insect frass, rodent droppings). Storage Manager signs pre-loading checklist confirming bin is clean and free of pests.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | Floors, storage areas | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Huller, cracker, sheller components | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading equipment, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
The establishment manager or nominated supervisor conducts a visual inspection of all cleaned areas prior to production commencement. Any deficiency identified is corrected before the area is cleared for use.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
At the most recent internal inspection (29 June 2025), all areas of Condamine Valley Grain Co-operative were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.

HACCP PLAN
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Plan
Tropical Farms Qld Pty Ltd | RE Number:   RE-SA-3015
Doc Ref:        TRO-HACCP-016
Version:        4.5
Date:             September 2024
State:            Victoria
1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Tropical Farms Qld Pty Ltd
Address: 16 Station Road, Victoria
Commodity: Chickpeas (Desi, Kabuli), Red Lentils
Scope: Receival, drying, cleaning, sizing, colour sorting and packing of chickpeas and lentils for export. Registered area RE-QLD-2891, Millmerran facility.
Intended use: Chickpeas for retail and food service. Red lentils for retail soup/curry packs. Destinations: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Middle East.
2. HACCP Team
Manager 16 (Quality Lead)
Operator 16A
Operator 16B
3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Receival / intake | Farm truck deliveries | Grain tipped into receival pit; probe sample for moisture, screenings
2 | Drying (chickpeas if >13% moisture) | Wet chickpeas | Dried to ≤12.5% moisture
3 | Bulk storage | Dry grain | Allocated to SILO-1 (chickpeas) or SILO-2 (lentils)
4 | Pre-cleaning | Stored grain | Pre-cleaner removes coarse trash and weed seeds
5 | Gravity separation | Pre-cleaned grain | Density separation removes immature seeds
6 | Sizing | Gravity-separated grain | Screened to export grade size
7 | Colour sorting | Sized grain | Optical colour sorter removes discoloured, mouldy seeds
8 | Packing | Sorted grain | Packed in 25 kg woven bags or 500 kg bulk bags
9 | Fumigation (if required) | Packed bags in sealed shed | Phosphine fumigation of export packs
10 | Dispatch | Fumigated packed goods | Loaded to container; dispatch docket signed
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1–3 | Chem | Mycotoxin (Aflatoxin, Ochratoxin A) from mould | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
1 | Chem | Pesticide MRL exceedance | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
4–7 | Phys | Foreign material — stones, metal, glass | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
5–6 | Bio | Insect infestation (bruchids, weevils) in storage | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
7 | Chem | Chemical cross-contact from colour sorter lubricants | 1 | 2 | 2 | — | GMP / PRP control
8–9 | Phys | Bag / bulk bag contamination (previous cargo) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
9 | Chem | Phosphine fumigant residue | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival/Storage | Mycotoxin | Intake moisture test; aeration; temperature probe; lab test on export lots | Aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg; OA ≤3 µg/kg | Moisture probe each lot; monthly temp probe; NATA test on flag lots | Monthly; per export consignment | Segregate; re-test; downgrade to feed if confirmed | Operations Manager
CCP-2 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; residue test on 5% of lots | MRL per India, Pakistan, Bangladesh (CODEX/strictest) | Spray records each grower; residue test flagged lots | Per grower/season | Quarantine; reject; notify grower; DAFF notification | Operations Manager
CCP-3 | Pre-cleaning/Sizing | Foreign material | Pre-cleaner + gravity table + optical sorter + metal detector | No metal >2 mm; no stones; no glass | Metal detector calibrated each shift; visual inspection each lot | Each shift | Stop line; remove contaminant; inspect; re-run | Operations Manager
CCP-4 | Fumigation | Phosphine residue | Licensed fumigator; ventilation protocol; residue test | ≤0.01 mg/kg at load-out | Licensed fumigator certificate; vent period checklist | Each fumigation event | Extend vent; re-test; do not load until cleared | Operations Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (DDPE-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of receival pit, conveyors, pre-cleaner, gravity table, colour sorter and packing lines.
• During season: colour sorter air nozzles cleaned daily; packing tables sanitised between shifts.
• Personnel: handwash on entry; no food in processing area; dust masks and gloves provided.
• Records: Cleaning Register (DDPE-CLN-01) signed after each event.
Waste Management Procedure (DDPE-WMP-001):
• Pre-cleaner trash / weed seeds: collected in sealed bins; removed to composting weekly.
• Dust: cyclone collector emptied weekly; disposed to composting.
• Reject bags: damaged or misprinted bags recycled through approved contractor.
• Chemical waste: fumigant containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (TRO-PCP-001):
• General pest controls described.
• No formal monitoring schedule or corrective action procedure documented.
• Pest effectiveness cannot be demonstrated without records.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
This HACCP plan does not include a documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch.

Specifically absent:
• No lot coding system for receival batches.
• No documented one-step-back / one-step-forward traceability procedure.
• No dispatch register linking packed bags to container and destination.
• No recall procedure or trace exercise schedule.

ACTION REQUIRED: Implement a Traceability System covering:
(a) Unique lot codes at receival; (b) Processing batch records; (c) Packing lot codes on bags;
(d) Dispatch register; (e) Annual trace exercise; (f) Recall activation protocol; (g) Record retention minimum 2 years.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.
Failed Goods Procedure (DDPE-FGP-001):
• Mycotoxin exceedance: lot placed on HOLD; re-test; if confirmed — downgrade to feed or destroy.
• Pesticide MRL failure: quarantine; reject export; notify grower; DAFF notified.
• Foreign material detection: stop line; remove contaminant; inspect batch; re-run.
• Non-conformance records maintained in DDPE-NCR register.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Tropical Farms Qld Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping

1.  OVERVIEW
Mid-North Lentil Growers is a registered export establishment located at 55 Barrier Highway, Clare SA 5453, SA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-SA-2021-0066 and is registered to handle and export Wheat under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
WB | Weighbridge + Control Room | 12×6 m | Steel portal, concrete pit | North entry — road access
RB | Receival Building | 30×18 m | Steel portal, smooth concrete floor | Centre-north of site
S1–S6 | Storage Silos ×6 (2,500 t ea) | Dia. 12 m | Galvanised steel on concrete ring beams | Central cluster
PL | Packing & Load-Out Shed | 28×18 m | Tilt-up concrete panels | South end of site
AM | Amenities Block | 8×5 m | Brick, self-contained | Adjacent to RB
CS | Chemical & Lubricant Store | 6×4 m | Steel, bunded slab | 15 m from PL
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 6×5 m | Enclosed steel room | Between RB and PL
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Grain augers | ×6 | Transfer and load-out
Belt conveyors (sealed) | ×3 | Receival to storage
Continuous-flow dryer | 1 unit | Moisture conditioning
Weighbridge system | 80 t rated | Inbound/outbound verification
Grain quality analyser (NIR) | In-line | Protein, moisture, oil testing
Rotary screen cleaner | 1 unit | Pre-storage cleaning
In-line belt sampler | 1 unit | Representative lot sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Wheat.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
Daylight hours provide adequate illumination through the open-sided design. Fixed lighting (two × 250 W metal halide fittings) is installed above the receival pit only. The packing hall, grading line and cool store loading area have no permanent overhead lighting — seasonal operations extend to dusk during peak harvest.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 2 toilets, 2 hand basins (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (3000 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1401 Rev 1): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Grain spillage | Sealed collection bins under auger/conveyor discharge | Daily removal
Grain dust | Cyclone separator → sealed collection bags | Fortnightly bag disposal
Washdown water | Floor drains → bunded sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste | Compressor baler in waste bay | Monthly contractor collection
Chemical containers | Labelled, sealed store | Licensed waste contractor quarterly
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated wheat residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).
8.  SERVICES
Service | Details
Electrical supply | Three-phase 415 V — SA Power Networks connection at site entry
Water supply | mains water — 50 mm service
Telecommunications | NBN fixed line + mobile backup at administration/control room
Sewerage | Licensed trade waste — EPA approval — serves amenities block
Stormwater | Graded hardstand to retention basin with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 200 kVA diesel generator — auto-start on grid failure

Refer to the establishment's General Food Safety and Quality Manual (Section 3) for standard cleaning and hygiene procedures. Establishment-specific adaptations are applied at the discretion of the site manager.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Almonds during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.

Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning.

Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.

At the most recent internal inspection (28 March 2025), all areas of Mid-North Lentil Growers were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to export sorghum (grain). Operations have expanded to include contract receival services for neighbouring farms, including weighbridge services, drying, and bagging for domestic sale. These contract activities are integrated with the export operation and use shared receival infrastructure.
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Sorghum receival | Registered sorghum intake for export | Within scope
Contract receival | Third-party receival services — weighbridge and intake | Not registered
Drying | High-temperature drying for domestic-grade product | Not registered
Bagging | Packaging into 25 kg bags for domestic distribution | Not registered
Dispatch | Export and domestic dispatch from shared dock | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-QLD-2022-0144 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 18 August 2022 and the current registration period extends to 17 August 2025. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Joshua Keller is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2013. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The establishment is located at 18 Rockhampton Road, Yeppoon QLD 4703. All export operations are conducted from the farm site. A site plan is maintained on file.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Mains connected
Water | Mains and tank water
Phone/internet | NBN connected
Weighbridge | Truck scale installed
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: sorghum is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of sorghum. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for Indonesia:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required; BARANTAN import permit conditions apply
Fumigation | Approved fumigation with supporting certificate
Aflatoxin | Total aflatoxin ≤15 ppb per BPOM regulations

HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Longreach Cattle & Grain Pty Ltd
Address: 90 Station Road, Tasmania
Commodity: Fresh Apples (Gala, Fuji), Fresh Pears (Packham)
Scope: Washing, grading, sizing, waxing, packing and cool storage of fresh apples and pears for export. Applicable to all operations within registered packhouse RE-QLD-0847.
Intended use: Fresh table fruit for retail sale. Destination: Singapore, Malaysia, UAE. Consuming population: general population including children.
2. HACCP Team
Manager 90 (Quality Lead)
Operator 90A
Operator 90B
3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Orchard receival | Field bins of apples/pears | Fruit received at packhouse loading dock
2 | Pre-cooling / dump tank | Received fruit | Pre-cooled to 4°C; hydro-cooled in chlorinated water
3 | Grading / sizing | Pre-cooled fruit | Graded by colour, size, defect (Greefa optical grader)
4 | Waxing (apples only) | Graded apples | Waxed with food-grade carnauba wax
5 | Packing | Graded/waxed fruit | Packed in retail trays or bulk cartons
6 | Metal detection | Packed cartons | Cartons passed through inline metal detector
7 | Cool storage | Packed cartons | Stored at 0–2°C / 95% RH; ethylene-controlled
8 | Dispatch | Cartons from cool store | Loaded to refrigerated transport under chain of cold
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1 | Chem | Pesticide residues exceeding importing country MRL | 3 | 3 | 9 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
1 | Bio | Codling moth (Cydia pomonella) live larvae | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
2 | Bio | Bacterial pathogens (Listeria) from dump water | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
3 | Phys | Glass / hard plastic from packhouse lighting / equipment | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
5–6 | Phys | Metal contamination from packing equipment | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
7 | Bio | Botrytis grey mould growth in cool store | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
7–8 | Phys | Temperature abuse — cold chain break | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-5 | See HACCP Control Chart
1 | Chem | Heavy metal contamination (orchard soil) | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Orchard Receival | Pesticide residue MRL | Spray diary review; NATA residue testing of consignment samples | MRL per importing country (Singapore SFA / UAE) | Spray records checked per grower per season; lab residue test on 10% of consignments | Each grower per season | Reject lot; quarantine; notify grower; notify DAFF | Food Safety Manager
CCP-2 | Orchard Receival | Codling moth live larvae | Visual inspection of fruit at intake; cold treatment protocol | Zero live larvae in consignment | Visual inspection 100 cartons per lot; cold treatment temperature log | Per lot | Reject consignment; notify DAFF; initiate cold disinfestation protocol | Food Safety Manager
CCP-3 | Pre-cooling / Dump Tank | Listeria spp. in dump water | Chlorinated dump water (50–200 ppm free chlorine); pH 6.5–7.5 | Free chlorine 50 ppm minimum; pH 6.5–7.5 | Chlorine + pH test strip every 2 hours; water changed every 4 hours | Every 2 hours | Correct chlorine level; discard non-compliant water batch; re-test | Packhouse Supervisor
CCP-4 | Metal Detection | Metal contamination | Inline metal detector: Fe ≥2.5 mm, non-Fe ≥3.0 mm, SS ≥3.5 mm | No metal detected above sensitivity limits | Detector sensitivity test hourly with test pieces; auto-reject of flagged cartons | Each carton (inline) | Quarantine flagged cartons; inspect; trace source of metal; re-run compliant cartons | Packhouse Supervisor
CCP-5 | Cool Storage / Dispatch | Temperature abuse | Continuous datalogger in each cool store cell; refrigerated dispatch vehicles | 0–2°C in store; ≤5°C in transport | Datalogger reading reviewed daily; dispatch vehicle pre-cool check | Continuous (logged) | If temp exceeds 5°C for >2 hrs: inspect product; reject if deteriorated; document | Food Safety Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (THF-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of packhouse — Greefa grader, conveyors, dump tank, wax applicator — using food-safe sanitiser (sodium hypochlorite 200 ppm).
• During season: dump tank water changed every 4 hours; brushes and pads cleaned daily.
• Personnel hygiene: mandatory handwash on entry; clean protective clothing (hairnets, gloves) required in packing area.
• Footwear: boot-wash stations at all packhouse entry points.
• Cleaning schedule: daily wipe-down of packing tables; weekly deep clean of grader lanes; signed Cleaning Register (THF-CLN-01).
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for the packhouse (pomace/peel, grading rejects, wastewater from dump tank, wax residue, packaging waste) are NOT included in this HACCP plan.
ACTION REQUIRED: Document waste streams, disposal methods, frequency and records in accordance with Rules s4-7A(2)(a) and DAFF Performance Standards Element 3.1.
Interim note: Packhouse rejects are currently collected by a local livestock farmer. No written procedure or records are maintained.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (THF-PCP-001):
• Rodent control: 12 external bait stations (Bromadiolone) around packhouse perimeter; inspected monthly.
• Insect: pheromone traps inside packhouse (6 traps — codling moth and oriental fruit moth); weekly monitoring.
• Bird exclusion: bird netting at all loading dock openings; doors kept closed during packing.
• Contracted pest controller: monthly site visit (Tasmanian Pest Control Services Pty Ltd); quarterly report.
• Records: Pest Control Log (THF-PC-01) signed monthly.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
Traceability System (THF-TRACE-001):
• Grower–lot–bin system: each field bin labelled with grower ID, orchard block, variety, harvest date.
• Packing records: each packing run assigned a lot code (grower–date–variety–run); printed on carton label.
• Dispatch: dispatch register links lot code → transport vehicle rego → cold store allocation → destination.
• Recall readiness: lot trace exercise conducted annually; 4-hour trace commitment.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
Failed Goods Procedure (THF-FGP-001):
• Lots failing pesticide residue test: placed on HOLD; grower notified; DAFF notified; lot destroyed or returned to grower for domestic use.
• Lots failing codling moth inspection: rejected from export; cold treatment applied; re-inspected before any re-presentation.
• Metal detector rejects: carton quarantined; inspected; source identified; disposed if contaminated.
• Records: all non-conformances logged in THF-NCR register.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Longreach Cattle & Grain Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).

1.  OVERVIEW
Capricorn Coast Grain is a registered export establishment located at 18 Rockhampton Road, Yeppoon QLD 4703, QLD. The establishment holds RE Number RE-QLD-2022-0144 and is registered to handle and export Cotton under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE

Packing/bagging line | 1 unit | Export preparation
Weighing system | In-line | Lot verification
In-line quality sampler | 1 unit | Representative sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Cotton.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
LED panel lighting installed 2015: 550 lux (processing), 440 lux (storage), 418 lux (load-out). IP65-rated food-grade fittings. Annual lux-level verification by licensed electrician.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Amenities block within 20 m of processing floor: 2 toilets, 2 hand basins hot/cold water, liquid soap, paper towels. Separate no-touch basin and hand sanitiser dispenser installed at cool store/packing area access point, as required by site hygiene protocol.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
All product-contact and grain-contact surfaces are smooth, non-porous and cleanable: 3-coat epoxy floor system; FRP (fibreglass-reinforced panel) wall linings to 2.7 m; stainless-steel equipment internals. Conveyor and auger housings have hinged access panels. Full washdown of product-contact surfaces required between commodity lots per cleaning SOP.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
The processing shed was purpose-built with full pest exclusion features. Several maintenance items have accumulated: roller door rubber threshold seals on doors 2 and 4 are worn with gaps of 8–22 mm; the cold store access door gasket has delaminated on the hinge side creating a 12 mm gap when closed; one south wall ventilation panel mesh has a 80×40 mm hole. These items are on the maintenance schedule.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Contained waste management infrastructure: liquid drains to bunded sump (4000 L) outside the processing building; solid waste in sealed wheeled bins with lids; external waste bay roofed and bunded on three sides with 300 mm concrete kerb and sealed slab. Organic waste composted in covered bay 50 m from processing. No open waste storage areas.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Establishment Waste Management Plan (EWMP v3.0, reviewed October 2025): details procedures for all waste streams — product spillage, packaging, liquid washdown, chemical containers and dust. Scheduled tasks on daily operations checklist, signed off by shift supervisor. Records retained 3 years minimum.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:

Product waste and screenings | Collection hoppers under cleaning unit | Daily removal
Grain dust | Bag filter or cyclone | Fortnightly
Washdown water | Drains → contained sump | Weekly
Packaging waste | Covered skip | Fortnightly contractor
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
The establishment is maintained in a clean and hygienic condition appropriate for export of Cotton. All product-contact surfaces are cleaned between commodity lots using the documented cleaning procedure. Non-product-contact surfaces cleaned on a 4-weekly schedule. No hygiene deficiencies at most recent inspection.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Pest condition assessment: Rodents: nil evidence in 6 months of monitoring. Grain insects: probe samples from all storage negative for live insects. Birds: no evidence of access to grain-contact areas. Last licensed fumigation: December 2024.

2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Capricorn Coast Grain used in nut processing and packing operations for export Macadamias. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Macadamias during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Rita Tran | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Area | After each intake | Remove nut debris, hulls, shells. Sweep floor and conveyor. Clear pit. | Dry sweep | Receival Staff | Intake record
Huller / Cracker / Sheller | After each run | Dismantle screens and access panels. Remove residue. Wipe rollers and blades. | BioDegreaser FD (1:25) + rinse | Processing Operator | Equipment cleaning log
Grading & Sizing Equipment | After each run | Clear product from screens. Brush surfaces. Wipe down conveyor belts and rollers. | EnzymeClear (1:20) | Grading Operator | Run record
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer | After each drying cycle | Remove nut skins and debris. Clean dryer mesh or tray surfaces. | Dry method | Drying Supervisor | Drying log
Storage Bins / Holding Area | Between commodity lots | Full physical sweep of bin walls and floor. Inspect for residue and pest signs. | Dry sweep | Storage Manager | Pre-loading checklist
Packing Line / Packaging Area | End of each shift | Remove nut fragments from conveyor, scales, packing tables. Sweep floor. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, basins, toilets, floors. Refill soap. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Area
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Huller / Cracker / Sheller
After each production run: Power off and lock out drive before opening. Dismantle outer access panels. Remove nut residue, shell fragments, and skin from rollers, screens, and internal surfaces using a stiff brush. Prepare BioDegreaser FD at 1:25. Apply to metal surfaces where oil residue is present. Contact time 5 minutes. Rinse with water. Allow to dry before reassembly. Record in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Grading & Sizing Equipment
After each run: Clear all nut product from grading screens and conveyor belts. Brush screens using designated nut-cleaning brush to remove embedded skins and fragments. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20 in a spray bottle. Spray conveyor belt and rollers. Wipe with clean cloth. Inspect for any remaining organic residue. Record in Run Record.
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Drying Area / Pads / Dryer in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Storage Bins / Holding Area
Between commodity lots: Inspect and clean storage bins before loading a new nut commodity. Using industrial vacuum, remove all residual nut material from bin walls, seams, and floor. Inspect for pest activity (insect frass, rodent droppings). Storage Manager signs pre-loading checklist confirming bin is clean and free of pests.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | Floors, storage areas | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
