EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading equipment, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Records are kept by the establishment manager. Location: manager's office. Staff are advised to confirm cleaning completion with the manager at the end of each shift.
Records are maintained in Mandarin as this reflects the primary working language of the processing workforce. Translation is available on request from the establishment manager.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template

9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Independent third-party hygiene audits are conducted twice annually. Between audits, internal verification is carried out by the establishment manager using a standardised checklist.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Non-conformances with cleaning requirements are recorded in the site's corrective action log. Root cause analysis is completed for any repeat event within 30 days. Completed corrective actions are verified by the manager and signed off before closure.

Routine inspection of Capricorn Coast Grain completed on 14 December 2025. All areas assessed as compliant with the hygiene standards required for the export of Macadamias. Cleaning logs current and records up to date.

CP1.evidence: Track 1 §2: contract receival, drying, bagging 'Not registered' but 'integrated with the export operation and use shared receival infrastructure'
CP1.reason: Unregistered contract activities are integrated with the export operation on shared receival infrastructure, so the establishment is operating beyond its registered operations.

CP2.evidence: Track 1 §3: 'There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration'
CP2.reason: No suspension is recorded against the registration or its operations.

CP3.evidence: Track 5 §1 registered export area (Lot 4 FP 12247) and Track 1 §5 area description with site plan
CP3.reason: The registered export area of the premises is documented in the site plan.

CP4.evidence: Track 5 §2-4 adjoining sites, buildings/structures and services
CP4.reason: Important features of the registered area, adjoining sites, buildings, facilities and services are documented.

CP5.evidence: Track 5 §5-6 export operations layout, permanent fixtures and equipment; schematic plan
CP5.reason: Layout of areas where export operations occur, including fixtures and equipment, is documented.

CP6.evidence: Track 1 §9: 'No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred'
CP6.reason: No notifiable changes to registration details occurred, with an undertaking to notify DAFF if any arise.

CP7.evidence: Track 1 §10: 'No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out'
CP7.reason: No physical alterations/extensions requiring approval are recorded (though operational scope expansion is captured under CP1).

CP8.evidence: Track 4 §2-4 buildings, equipment, facilities and services listed
CP8.reason: The establishment has the buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for its export operations.

CP9.evidence: Track 4 §4.2: LED lighting 550/440/418 lux, annual lux verification
CP9.reason: Adequate lighting is provided and verified.

CP10.evidence: Track 4 §4.3: amenities block with 2 toilets, 2 hand basins hot/cold, soap, paper towels
CP10.reason: Hand washing and toilet facilities are provided.

CP11.evidence: Track 4 §5.1: epoxy floors, FRP linings, stainless internals, hinged access panels
CP11.reason: Design and construction allow effective cleaning of buildings, equipment and facilities.

CP12.evidence: Track 4 §5.2: roller door seals worn with 8-22 mm gaps, cold store gasket 12 mm gap, ventilation mesh 80x40 mm hole
CP12.reason: Worn door seals and a mesh hole compromise pest exclusion, failing the minimisation of contamination, infestation and pest harbourage.

CP13.evidence: Track 4 §5.3: bunded sump, sealed lidded bins, roofed/bunded waste bay, no open waste storage
CP13.reason: Design provides efficient and hygienic disposal of solid and liquid waste.

CP14.evidence: Track 5 §7: DAFF Inspection Bay with stainless bench 2.1x0.8 m, 550 lux, handwash, probe set, sample fridge
CP14.reason: Inspection area and equipment are designed for AO sample collection and inspection, including an inspection bench.

CP15.evidence: Track 4 §3: cleaning and separation unit (pre-storage cleaning); Track 5 grading/optical sorter with rejects to waste
CP15.reason: Cleaning/separation and grading equipment manage the risk of large contaminants.

CP16.evidence: Track 4 §3 cleaning/separation unit; Track 5 §5 grading/sorting rejects to waste bin
CP16.reason: Screening equipment removes large contaminants from the product.

CP17.evidence: Track 6 Hygiene & Sanitation Plan with master cleaning schedule and SOPs
CP17.reason: A documented system of controls to manage hygiene exists.

CP18.evidence: Track 2 §6: '[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED] Waste management procedures ... are NOT included ... No written procedure or records are maintained'
CP18.reason: The HACCP plan explicitly documents that waste procedures and records are not maintained, revealing a gap in the waste-control system (conflicts with Track 4 EWMP).

CP19.evidence: Track 6 hygiene controls and Track 4 §6 EWMP appropriate for grain operations
CP19.reason: The hygiene/waste controls that are documented are broadly effective for the type of operations.

CP20.evidence: Track 3 bait station register, Track 7 21-station map, Track 2 §7 pest program
CP20.reason: A system of controls to manage pests including rodent bait stations is in place.

CP21.evidence: Track 7 §1: 'Trend review shows low activity with completed escalation actions and closure evidence'
CP21.reason: The pest control system is effective for the operations, with monitoring and closure evidence.

CP22.evidence: Track 3: 'Records retained from 2025 (< 2 years — NON-COMPLIANT (C3))'; new establishment registered Oct 2024
CP22.reason: Less than 2 years of hygiene/waste/pest records are retained.

CP23.reason: Hygiene records are kept in Mandarin, failing the requirement that records be in English.

CP24.evidence: Track 4 §7.1 'No hygiene deficiencies at most recent inspection'; Track 6 §11 all areas compliant
CP24.reason: Areas are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition (minor debris in non-operational corners noted in Track 7).

CP25.evidence: Track 4 §7.2 nil rodent evidence, negative insect probes; Track 3 no infestation detected
CP25.reason: Areas are maintained so prescribed goods are not likely to be infested or contaminated.

CP26.evidence: Track 7 §2: BS-05 and BS-10 'Loose anchor'; BS-15 and BS-20 'Water ingress'
CP26.reason: Several bait stations are not in good working order, failing the fit-for-purpose requirement.

CP27.evidence: Track 7 §4: 'Temporary overflow pesticide cartons held in open shelf area during stocktake'
CP27.reason: Pesticide stored on open shelving creates a contamination risk to prescribed products.

CP28.evidence: Track 7 §4: 'Chemical storage physically separated from export product handling and preparation areas'; Track 3 chemicals in separate shed 20 m from pit
CP28.reason: Chemical storage is stated to be physically separated from product preparation areas.

CP29.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 1 Receival Register with property/paddock ID, variety, grade, received by
CP29.reason: Traceability from the source property to receival is documented.

CP30.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 2 Product Movement Log with source/destination silos and ledger cross-checks
CP30.reason: Traceability while goods are at the establishment is maintained.

CP31.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 4 Dispatch/Transfer Dockets with destination premises and Dest RE No.
CP31.reason: Traceability to the next premises is documented.

CP32.evidence: Track 2 §8 traceability system (grower-lot-bin, lot codes) and Track 9 registers
CP32.reason: Systems of controls (labelling, record keeping) maintain traceability and integrity.

CP33.evidence: Track 8 §2: 'Flow chart omits one alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods'
CP33.reason: The product flow chart omits a transfer path, so it does not fully demonstrate product movement/integrity.

CP34.evidence: Track 2 §9 Failed Goods Procedure; Track 9 Sheet 6 Rejected Goods Log
CP34.reason: A system of controls to manage failed/rejected goods including treatment and re-presentation exists.

CP35.evidence: Track 8 §1 'temporary mesh segregation pending permanent barrier'; Track 2 §10 '[DEFICIENCY] No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch'
CP35.reason: Contamination/infestation controls are incomplete (interim mesh barrier; no documented re-contamination controls).

CP36.evidence: Track 8 §3: 'Substitution controls rely on single-operator checks for selected late-shift dispatches'
CP36.reason: Single-operator dispatch checks create a substitution risk, failing the minimisation of substitution.

CP37.evidence: Track 8 §4: 'Occasional packaging QC records attached to shift summary instead of individual lot files'
CP37.reason: Packaging QC is performed and met; the noted issue is record filing rather than a packaging-requirement failure.

CP38.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 7: 'Jan 2025 - current', 'Legacy index migration in progress'
CP38.reason: Traceability records span under 2 years and migration is incomplete, failing the 2-year retention requirement.

CP39.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 6 'blending rationale logged in shift note only'; Sheet 7 'Rejected-goods attachments partly offsite', from 2025
CP39.reason: Rejected/failed-goods records are under 2 years and blending rationale is not properly retained.

CP40.evidence: Track 9 registers are in English with dates for each action
CP40.reason: Traceability records are in English and dated (completeness issues addressed under CP38/CP39).

CP41.evidence: Track 1 §11 Indonesia requirements (PC, fumigation cert, aflatoxin ≤15 ppb); Track 9 fumigation treatment records
CP41.reason: Importing country requirements are documented and addressed with supporting treatment records.

1. Establishment Details
Business Name | Albury Grain and Storage Pty Ltd
Trading Name | Albury Grain and Storage Pty Ltd
Address | 100 Hume Highway, Albury NSW 2640
State/Territory | NSW
Contact Person | Carl Abramson

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Barley receival | Intake of bulk and bagged barley from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of barley to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of barley in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-NSW-2021-0044 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 9 February 2021 and the current registration period extends to 8 February 2024. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Carl Abramson is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2016. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 19 on Plan DP 349232, located at 100 Hume Highway, Albury NSW 2640. The total registered area is 38.5 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for Saudi Arabia:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary | Phytosanitary requirements apply
Fumigation | Fumigation may be required
Certificates | Relevant certificates to be provided
12. Supporting Documents
Farm Site Plan (Appendix A)
HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

HACCP PLAN
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Plan
Maranoa Farms Pty Ltd | RE Number:   RE-VIC-3050
Doc Ref:        MAR-HACCP-051
Version:        3.0
Date:             April 2026
State:            Victoria
1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Maranoa Farms Pty Ltd
Address: 51 Station Road, Victoria
Commodity: Canola ( export grade ), Linseed
Scope: Receival, storage, cleaning and bulk loading of canola and linseed for export. Cold pressing of linseed oil (in-line). Registered area RE-NSW-1882, Kwinana facility.
Intended use: Canola for crushing/oil extraction. Linseed oil for food and industrial use. Destination: Japan (canola), Germany (linseed oil). Non-GM canola for EU markets.
2. HACCP Team
Manager 51 (Quality Lead)
Operator 51A
Operator 51B
3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Paddock planning & variety selection | Variety/agronomy plans | Seed selection — GM-status documented
2 | Harvest & field transport | Standing crop | Harvested oilseed at receival pit
3 | Receival / intake testing | Bulk oilseed | Oil content, moisture, impurities tested at intake
4 | Drying / conditioning | Wet grain (>9% moisture) | Dried oilseed ≤8% moisture
5 | Storage | Dry oilseed | Stored in designated silo — GM and non-GM segregated
6 | Cleaning / scalping | Stored oilseed | Cleaned of trash, weed seeds and foreign material
7 | Cold pressing (linseed only) | Clean linseed | Linseed oil extracted; meal collected
8 | Bulk loading (canola) | Cleaned canola | Loaded to bulk vessel via pneumatic conveyor
9 | Tanker filling (linseed oil) | Pressed linseed oil | Filled to food-grade tanker
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1–2 | Chem | Glucosinolates above export spec (canola) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
1–2 | Chem | Erucic acid above EU limit (0.5%) — old varieties | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
1 | Chem | Pesticide MRL exceedance — herbicide, fungicide | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
3–5 | Chem | Mycotoxin (Ochratoxin A, aflatoxin) from wet/damaged seed | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
5 | Bio | Insect infestation (grain weevils, beetles) in storage | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Bio | Rodent infestation in silos | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
6 | Phys | Foreign material — stones, steel, glass | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
7 | Chem | PAH contamination from pressing equipment (lubricants) | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
8–9 | Phys | Transport unit/tanker contamination (previous cargo) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Chem | GM cross-contamination of non-GM lots (Identity Preservation) | 3 | 3 | 9 | CCP-5 | See HACCP Control Chart
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; residue test on flag lots | MRL per Japan / EU Regulation 396/2005 | Spray records checked each grower per harvest; residue test 5% of receival lots | Per grower/season | Reject lot; quarantine; grower notified; DAFF notified | QA Manager
CCP-2 | Storage | Mycotoxin | Moisture monitoring; aeration; temperature probe | OA ≤3 µg/kg; aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg | Intake moisture test; monthly temperature probe; lab test on export lots | Monthly during storage; per export consignment | Segregate affected silo; test; downgrade or destroy if above threshold | QA Manager
CCP-3 | Storage | Rodent infestation | 16 perimeter bait stations; monthly inspection | No visible live rodents or fresh signs in storage zone | Monthly bait station inspection (Form AOW-PC-01); pitfall traps quarterly | Monthly | Engage licensed contractor immediately; quarantine affected silo | Plant Manager
CCP-4 | Cleaning/Scalping | Foreign material | Scalper (6 mm screen), rare-earth magnetic separator | No metal > 2 mm; no glass; no hard foreign matter | Scalper screen inspection each shift; magnet cleaning log | Each shift | Stop line; remove contaminant; inspect product; re-screen | Plant Manager
CCP-5 | Storage/Loading | GM cross-contamination | Dedicated IP silos for non-GM; flush/cleanout procedures; GM test on non-GM lots | <0.9% adventitious GM presence (EU threshold) | PCR test on non-GM lots at receival and pre-shipment | Per non-GM lot | Reject non-GM classification; re-test; notify customer | QA Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (AOW-HSP-001):
• Equipment cleaning: pressing equipment (linseed press, conveyors) cleaned with food-safe degreaser between product changes.
• Silo interiors cleaned by air-sweep before new season intake.
• Personnel hygiene: access control to processing area; no food or drink in processing zone.
• Oil tanker hygiene: tanker interior inspected and swabbed before filling; HACCP tanker form completed.
• Records: Cleaning Register (AOW-CLN-01) signed after each event.
Waste Management Procedure (AOW-WMP-001):
• Scalper screenings / trash: collected in sealed bins; transported off-site to approved composting.
• Oilseed dust: cyclone dust collector; dust collected in sealed bags; removed weekly.
• Linseed meal (pressing by-product): sold to livestock feed market; removed within 48 hours of pressing.
• Chemical waste: fumigant and pesticide containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
• Wastewater from cleaning: directed to grease trap; collected by liquid waste contractor monthly.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (AOW-PCP-001):
• Rodents: 16 perimeter bait stations (Bromadiolone); monthly inspection; licensed contractor annual review.
• Insects: pitfall traps in each silo; grain temperature probe weekly in storage season; phosphine fumigation when insects detected.
• Bird exclusion: all structural openings sealed; netting at loading conveyor ends.
• Records: Pest Control Log (AOW-PC-01) monthly.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Maranoa Farms Pty Ltd. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
Failed Goods Procedure (AOW-FGP-001):
• GM contamination above threshold: lot re-classified as non-Identity Preserved; customer notified; DAFF notified.
• Mycotoxin exceedance: silo placed on HOLD; re-test from secondary sample; if confirmed, dispose to non-food use.
• Pesticide MRL: reject export consignment; segregate; grower liability documented; option to process to domestic oil (if MRL met under FSANZ).
• All non-conformances recorded in AOW-NCR register with root cause analysis.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
Phytosanitary Security (AOW-PSP-001):
• Export-cleared grain stored in dedicated silos; not accessible to uncleared grain.
• Identity Preserved (non-GM) lots in dedicated, clearly labelled IP silos.
• Loading procedure: transport unit inspected before loading; last cargo record reviewed; sealed containers sealed at point of loading.
• DAFF sampling completed before loading of each export lot.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

1.  OVERVIEW
Albury Grain and Storage is a registered export establishment located at 100 Hume Highway, Albury NSW 2640, NSW. The establishment holds RE Number RE-NSW-2021-0044 and is registered to handle and export Chickpeas under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
WB | Weighbridge | 40 t pit type | Concrete pit, steel deck | North entry
GS | Grading Shed | 28×20 m | Steel portal, concrete floor | Centre of site
S1–S4 | Storage Bins ×4 (1,000 t ea) | Dia. 10 m | Steel on concrete | South cluster
AM | Amenities Block | 7×5 m | Brick | Adjacent GS entry
CH | Chemical Store | 5×3 m | Steel, bunded | Remote — NW corner
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 5×4 m | Enclosed room in GS | GS north end
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Pulse grader (aspiration screen) | 1 unit | Cleaning and grading
Destoner | 1 unit | Foreign material removal
Colour sorter | 1 unit | Quality grading
Bagging machine (25 kg bags) | 1 unit | Bulk export bagging
Weighbridge system | 40 t rated | Truck weighing
In-line sampler | 1 unit | Representative lot sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Chickpeas.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 520 lux packing hall, 400 lux cool store entry, 380 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-159, version 2.4, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Pulse screenings and tailings | Collection bins under aspirator — sealed | Daily removal
Dust and chaff | Bag filter on aspiration system | Weekly bag disposal
Washdown water | Floor drains → sediment sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste (bags, strapping) | Skip in external waste bay | Fortnightly collection
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 8 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Pheromone trap monitoring in the chickpeas packing hall has detected elevated catches of Indian meal moth (Plodia interpunctella). Current catch rate: 42 moths/trap/week (investigation threshold: 10). Treatment plan being prepared by licensed pest management contractor. Live larvae found in one product sample during quality inspection.
8.  SERVICES
Service | Details
Electrical supply | Three-phase 415 V — NSW Power Networks connection at site entry
Water supply | mains water — 32 mm service
Telecommunications | NBN fixed line + mobile backup at administration/control room
Sewerage | Septic system — licensed — serves amenities block
Stormwater | Sheet flow to soakage trench with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 60 kVA generator — auto-start on grid failure

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1.  ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
Establishment Name | Albury Grain and Storage
RE Number | RE-NSW-2021-0044
State / Territory | NSW
Property Address | 100 Hume Highway, Albury NSW 2640
Registered Commodity | Mixed Berries
Operation Type | Hort
Responsible Officer | Rosa De Luca
Property Area | 55.0 ha
Document Version | 3.5
Plan Date | 11 January 2025
Next Review | 11 January 2027
Policy Context | Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021 / DAFF IMLS-12-3742 Element 3
2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Albury Grain and Storage used in horticultural packing and cold-chain export operations for Mixed Berries. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Mixed Berries during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Rosa De Luca | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay | After each intake | Remove packaging, debris, organic material. Wash floor with pressure hose. | ProClean 200 (1:50) + rinse | Receival Operator | Intake log sign-off
Grading & Sorting Line | After each run / Daily | Remove product residue from conveyor belts, rollers, brushes. Wipe down all surfaces. | EnzymeClear Organic Remover (1:20) | Line Supervisor | Grading log
Packing Area / Line | End of each shift | Clear line of product. Sweep floor. Clean packing tables and equipment surfaces. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning record
Cold Storage / Coolrooms | Monthly / Between loads | Defrost and clean evaporator coils. Wipe walls, shelves, floor. Check drain. | AcidRinse 500 (1:50) + QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Cold Store Manager | Cold store maintenance log
Pre-Cool Chamber | Weekly | Wipe walls and shelving. Check air circulation unit and drain for organic buildup. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Operations Staff | Weekly inspection log
Loading Dock / Dispatch | After each dispatch run | Remove packaging waste. Sweep dock floor. Check refrigerated transport door seal. | Dry sweep + spot clean | Dispatch Supervisor | Dispatch checklist
Floor Drains (all areas) | Weekly | Remove covers. Flush with hot water and cleaning agent. Scrub drain channels. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Maintenance | Drain cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Mop floors. Clean basins and toilets. Wipe all surfaces. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff / rostered | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay
After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line
After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line
End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms
Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | General floors, dock surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading line, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
AcidRinse 500 Descaler | AgriChem Aust | Acidic cleaner | 1:50 in water | Coolroom coils, drain channels | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Machinery, conveyor chain | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Paper-based cleaning records are maintained in a ring-binder located at the site office. Completed records are filed monthly and stored for at least two years.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
ATP (adenosine triphosphate) swab testing is used monthly on critical food-contact surfaces to verify cleaning efficacy. Results are recorded in the Surface Hygiene Register alongside the cleaning log.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Albury Grain and Storage (conducted 11 January 2025) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.
12.  REVIEW AND AUTHORISATION

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Barley receival | Intake of bulk and bagged barley from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of barley to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of barley in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-VIC-2020-0093 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 20 August 2020 and the current registration period extends to 19 August 2023. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Robert Mackenzie is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2008. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 50 on Plan DP 703173, located at 152 Western Highway, Horsham VIC 3400. The total registered area is 84.2 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 8,000 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for Japan:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required; declare freedom from stripe rust, Tilletia spp. and listed nematodes
Residue Compliance | Pesticide residues must comply with Japan's Positive List System
Pre-clearance | MAFF pre-clearance inspection may be required for high-risk consignments
Mycotoxin Limits | Aflatoxin B1 ≤10 ppb; DON ≤1,100 ppb for wheat
12. Supporting Documents

HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

HACCP PLAN
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Plan
Avocet Oilseeds (VIC) Pty Ltd | RE Number:   RE-VIC-1882
Doc Ref:        AOW-HACCP-003
Version:        1.4

State:            Western Australia
1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Avocet Oilseeds (VIC) Pty Ltd
Address: Lot 12 Kwinana Industrial Strip, Kwinana VIC 6167
Commodity: Canola (TruFlex GM, APO grade), Linseed (export standard)
Scope: Receival, storage, cleaning and bulk loading of canola and linseed for export. Cold pressing of linseed oil (in-line). Registered area RE-VIC-1882, Kwinana facility.
Intended use: Canola for crushing/oil extraction. Linseed oil for food and industrial use. Destination: Japan (canola), Germany (linseed oil). Non-GM canola for EU markets.
2. HACCP Team
Robert Stanhope (QA Manager — Lead)
Gavin Ngo (Plant Manager)
Sarah Wilkins (Lab Analyst)
Prof. David Chu (HACCP Consultant, Murdoch Univ.)
3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Paddock planning & variety selection | Variety/agronomy plans | Seed selection — GM-status documented
2 | Harvest & field transport | Standing crop | Harvested oilseed at receival pit
3 | Receival / intake testing | Bulk oilseed | Oil content, moisture, impurities tested at intake
4 | Drying / conditioning | Wet grain (>9% moisture) | Dried oilseed ≤8% moisture
5 | Storage | Dry oilseed | Stored in designated silo — GM and non-GM segregated
6 | Cleaning / scalping | Stored oilseed | Cleaned of trash, weed seeds and foreign material
7 | Cold pressing (linseed only) | Clean linseed | Linseed oil extracted; meal collected
8 | Bulk loading (canola) | Cleaned canola | Loaded to bulk vessel via pneumatic conveyor
9 | Tanker filling (linseed oil) | Pressed linseed oil | Filled to food-grade tanker
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1–2 | Chem | Glucosinolates above export spec (canola) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
1–2 | Chem | Erucic acid above EU limit (0.5%) — old varieties | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
1 | Chem | Pesticide MRL exceedance — herbicide, fungicide | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
3–5 | Chem | Mycotoxin (Ochratoxin A, aflatoxin) from wet/damaged seed | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
5 | Bio | Insect infestation (grain weevils, beetles) in storage | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Bio | Rodent infestation in silos | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
6 | Phys | Foreign material — stones, steel, glass | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
7 | Chem | PAH contamination from pressing equipment (lubricants) | 1 | 3 | 3 | — | GMP / PRP control
8–9 | Phys | Transport unit/tanker contamination (previous cargo) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Chem | GM cross-contamination of non-GM lots (Identity Preservation) | 3 | 3 | 9 | CCP-5 | See HACCP Control Chart
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; residue test on flag lots | MRL per Japan / EU Regulation 396/2005 | Spray records checked each grower per harvest; residue test 5% of receival lots | Per grower/season | Reject lot; quarantine; grower notified; DAFF notified | QA Manager
CCP-2 | Storage | Mycotoxin | Moisture monitoring; aeration; temperature probe | OA ≤3 µg/kg; aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg | Intake moisture test; monthly temperature probe; lab test on export lots | Monthly during storage; per export consignment | Segregate affected silo; test; downgrade or destroy if above threshold | QA Manager
CCP-3 | Storage | Rodent infestation | 16 perimeter bait stations; monthly inspection | No visible live rodents or fresh signs in storage zone | Monthly bait station inspection (Form AOW-PC-01); pitfall traps quarterly | Monthly | Engage licensed contractor immediately; quarantine affected silo | Plant Manager
CCP-4 | Cleaning/Scalping | Foreign material | Scalper (6 mm screen), rare-earth magnetic separator | No metal > 2 mm; no glass; no hard foreign matter | Scalper screen inspection each shift; magnet cleaning log | Each shift | Stop line; remove contaminant; inspect product; re-screen | Plant Manager
CCP-5 | Storage/Loading | GM cross-contamination | Dedicated IP silos for non-GM; flush/cleanout procedures; GM test on non-GM lots | <0.9% adventitious GM presence (EU threshold) | PCR test on non-GM lots at receival and pre-shipment | Per non-GM lot | Reject non-GM classification; re-test; notify customer | QA Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (AOW-HSP-001):
• Equipment cleaning: pressing equipment (linseed press, conveyors) cleaned with food-safe degreaser between product changes.
• Silo interiors cleaned by air-sweep before new season intake.
• Personnel hygiene: access control to processing area; no food or drink in processing zone.
• Oil tanker hygiene: tanker interior inspected and swabbed before filling; HACCP tanker form completed.
• Records: Cleaning Register (AOW-CLN-01) signed after each event.
Waste Management Procedure (AOW-WMP-001):
• Scalper screenings / trash: collected in sealed bins; transported off-site to approved composting.
• Oilseed dust: cyclone dust collector; dust collected in sealed bags; removed weekly.
• Linseed meal (pressing by-product): sold to livestock feed market; removed within 48 hours of pressing.
• Chemical waste: fumigant and pesticide containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
• Wastewater from cleaning: directed to grease trap; collected by liquid waste contractor monthly.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (AOW-PCP-001):
• Rodents: 16 perimeter bait stations (Bromadiolone); monthly inspection; licensed contractor annual review.
• Insects: pitfall traps in each silo; grain temperature probe weekly in storage season; phosphine fumigation when insects detected.
• Bird exclusion: all structural openings sealed; netting at loading conveyor ends.
• Records: Pest Control Log (AOW-PC-01) monthly.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
Traceability System (AOW-TRACE-001):
• Each silo assigned unique ID (silo number + commodity + IP/non-GM status + season).
• Receival dockets link grower → farm block → variety → quantity → silo.
• Dispatch: bill of lading links silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination.
• GM testing records linked to lot reference; retained 5 years (EU requirement).
• One-step-forward / one-step-back trace exercise performed semi-annually.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.
Failed Goods Procedure (AOW-FGP-001):
• GM contamination above threshold: lot re-classified as non-Identity Preserved; customer notified; DAFF notified.
• Mycotoxin exceedance: silo placed on HOLD; re-test from secondary sample; if confirmed, dispose to non-food use.
• Pesticide MRL: reject export consignment; segregate; grower liability documented; option to process to domestic oil (if MRL met under FSANZ).
• All non-conformances recorded in AOW-NCR register with root cause analysis.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
Phytosanitary Security (AOW-PSP-001):
• Export-cleared grain stored in dedicated silos; not accessible to uncleared grain.
• Identity Preserved (non-GM) lots in dedicated, clearly labelled IP silos.

1.  OVERVIEW
Grampians Grain Trust is a registered export establishment located at 152 Western Highway, Horsham VIC 3400, VIC. The establishment holds RE Number RE-VIC-2020-0093 and is registered to handle and export Canola under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE

3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose

Rotary screen cleaner | 1 unit | Pre-storage cleaning
In-line belt sampler | 1 unit | Representative lot sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Canola.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 470 lux packing hall, 360 lux cool store entry, 342 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-103, version 2.3, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Grain spillage | Sealed collection bins under auger/conveyor discharge | Daily removal
Grain dust | Cyclone separator → sealed collection bags | Fortnightly bag disposal
Washdown water | Floor drains → bunded sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste | Compressor baler in waste bay | Monthly contractor collection
Chemical containers | Labelled, sealed store | Licensed waste contractor quarterly
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 4 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: January 2025).

2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Grampians Grain Trust used in horticultural packing and cold-chain export operations for Mangoes. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Mangoes during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Lee Chandra | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay | After each intake | Remove packaging, debris, organic material. Wash floor with pressure hose. | ProClean 200 (1:50) + rinse | Receival Operator | Intake log sign-off
Grading & Sorting Line | After each run / Daily | Remove product residue from conveyor belts, rollers, brushes. Wipe down all surfaces. | EnzymeClear Organic Remover (1:20) | Line Supervisor | Grading log
Packing Area / Line | End of each shift | Clear line of product. Sweep floor. Clean packing tables and equipment surfaces. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning record
Cold Storage / Coolrooms | Monthly / Between loads | Defrost and clean evaporator coils. Wipe walls, shelves, floor. Check drain. | AcidRinse 500 (1:50) + QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Cold Store Manager | Cold store maintenance log
Pre-Cool Chamber | Weekly | Wipe walls and shelving. Check air circulation unit and drain for organic buildup. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Operations Staff | Weekly inspection log
Loading Dock / Dispatch | After each dispatch run | Remove packaging waste. Sweep dock floor. Check refrigerated transport door seal. | Dry sweep + spot clean | Dispatch Supervisor | Dispatch checklist
Floor Drains (all areas) | Weekly | Remove covers. Flush with hot water and cleaning agent. Scrub drain channels. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Maintenance | Drain cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Mop floors. Clean basins and toilets. Wipe all surfaces. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff / rostered | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay
After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line
After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line
End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms
Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | General floors, dock surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading line, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
AcidRinse 500 Descaler | AgriChem Aust | Acidic cleaner | 1:50 in water | Coolroom coils, drain channels | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Machinery, conveyor chain | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Independent third-party hygiene audits are conducted twice annually. Between audits, internal verification is carried out by the establishment manager using a standardised checklist.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Grampians Grain Trust (conducted 15 September 2024) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Barley receival | Intake of bulk and bagged barley from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of barley to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of barley in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-SA-2020-0120 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 28 November 2020 and the current registration period extends to 27 November 2023. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
James Okoye is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2017. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 19 on Plan DP 207531, located at 99 Port Wakefield Road, Two Wells SA 5501. The total registered area is 28.9 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 1,200 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for Saudi Arabia:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required; SFDA import permit conditions apply
Fumigation | Methyl bromide or approved alternative; certificate with consignment
Residue Limits | Comply with Saudi SFDA MRL requirements
Labelling | Arabic labelling of commodity, origin and weight required
12. Supporting Documents

HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

Step | Process | Input | Output

4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary

CCP-1 | Receival | Mycotoxin (Fumonisins/AFB1) | Intake mycotoxin rapid test; lab confirmation | Fumonisins ≤2,000 µg/kg (EU); AFB1 ≤2 µg/kg | Rapid test on each receival lot (RidaQuick strip); NATA lab confirmation on flag | Each lot at intake | Reject lot; quarantine; notify grower; DAFF notification | Quality Coordinator
CCP-2 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review; residue testing on flagged lots | MRL per Mexico / Indonesia (Codex defaults) | Spray records checked per grower; residue test 5% of lots | Per grower/season | Quarantine; reject; notify grower | Quality Coordinator

6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (NQGT-HSP-001):
• Terminal cleaning: receival pit cleaned weekly; conveyor gallery swept daily; elevator boots washed monthly.
• Between commodities: blow-down of all conveyors and elevator legs before changing grain type.
• Vessel loading spout cleaned after each vessel loading.
• Personnel: safety footwear and dust masks required in operational areas; handwash on entry.
• Records: Cleaning Register (NQGT-CLN-01).
Waste Management Procedure (NQGT-WMP-001):
• Screenings: scalper waste in sealed skip; removed by contractor to composting monthly.
• Grain dust: cyclone collector emptied weekly; removed to composting.
• Vessel hold washings: water + grain residues pumped to shore reception; disposed per port environmental regulations.
• Chemical waste: fumigant sachets disposed per APVMA requirements.

• Records: Non-Conformance Register (NQGT-NCR-01).

• Post-fumigation grain not moved until DAFF sampling complete.

1.  OVERVIEW
Adelaide Plains Grain is a registered export establishment located at 99 Port Wakefield Road, Two Wells SA 5501, SA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-SA-2020-0120 and is registered to handle and export Table Grapes under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
RB | Receival & Processing Building | 40×25 m | Steel/concrete | Centre of site
S1–S6 | Storage Bins | Dia. 12 m | Galv. steel | South cluster
PL | Packing & Dispatch Shed | 35×20 m | Tilt-up concrete | SE corner
AM | Amenities Block | 9×5 m | Brick | Adjacent RB
CH | Chemical Store | 6×4 m | Steel, bunded | NW corner
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 6×5 m | Enclosed room | RB north end
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Receival pit and elevator | 1 unit | Primary receival
Cleaning and separation unit | 1 unit | Pre-storage cleaning
Drying system | batch | Moisture reduction
Packing/bagging line | 1 unit | Export preparation
Weighing system | In-line | Lot verification
In-line quality sampler | 1 unit | Representative sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Table Grapes.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 500 lux processing, 400 lux storage, 380 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (1500 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6.  SASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1801 Rev 1): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Product waste and screenings | Collection hoppers under cleaning unit | Daily removal
Grain dust | Bag filter or cyclone | Fortnightly
Washdown water | Drains → contained sump | Weekly
Packaging waste | Covered skip | Fortnightly contractor
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated table grapes residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).
8.  SERVICES

1.  ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
