2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Adelaide Plains Grain used in specialty crop processing and export preparation for Table Grapes. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Table Grapes during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Irene Walsh | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Area | After each intake | Remove product debris, packaging material. Sweep or vacuum floor and equipment. | Dry method | Receival Operator | Intake record
Processing Equipment / Line | After each production run | Clean rollers, screens, belts. Remove product residue from all contact surfaces. | ProClean 200 (1:50) or BioDegreaser FD (1:25) | Processing Operator | Equipment log
Drying / Conditioning Area | After each cycle | Remove product residue from drying surfaces and screens. Check for accumulation. | Dry brush + compressed air | Drying Supervisor | Drying record
Storage / Holding Area | Between commodity lots | Full sweep-out of storage space. Inspect for residue and pest activity. | Dry method | Storage Manager | Pre-loading checklist
Packing & Export Preparation Area | End of each shift | Clear product from all surfaces. Sweep floor. Wipe all equipment. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, floors, basins, toilets. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Area
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Processing Equipment / Line
After each production run: Isolate equipment before cleaning. Remove product residue from all contact surfaces: rollers, belts, screens. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to surfaces, contact time 3 minutes, rinse with clean water. For heavily soiled components, use BioDegreaser FD at 1:25 prior to main clean. Inspect all surfaces for residue before returning to production. Record in Equipment Log.
Drying / Conditioning Area
After each drying cycle: Allow drying surfaces to cool before cleaning. Use a stiff brush and compressed air to remove product residue and fines from drying mesh, trays, or belts. Vacuum accumulated material from under dryer frame. Inspect moisture sensing equipment surfaces. Record in Drying Record.
Storage / Holding Area
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Storage / Holding Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Packing & Export Preparation Area
End of each shift: Clear all product from packing tables and export staging area. Remove used packaging materials to waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Confirm area is clear and clean before locking up. Record in Shift Cleaning Log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Product fines and residues accumulate in transition points, screen joins, and under drying surfaces. These dead zones are addressed during each production run clean-down and inspected during the weekly walkthrough.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | General floors, surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Processing equipment | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Each area supervisor completes a sign-off on the shift cleaning record, confirming that cleaning has been carried out to the required standard. The site manager reviews all records at the end of each production day.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
At the most recent internal inspection (30 July 2025), all areas of Adelaide Plains Grain were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.

1. Establishment Details
Business Name | Gwydir Valley Grain Trust
Trading Name | Gwydir Valley Grain Trust

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to export barley (grain). Current season operations have focused primarily on wheat accumulation and storage following favourable local harvest conditions. A small volume of barley has also been received and is held in silo 3.
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Wheat receival | Intake of wheat — dominant activity this season | Not registered
Barley receival | Limited intake of barley this season | Within scope
Storage | Co-storage of wheat and barley in shared silo complex | Not registered
Dispatch | Loading of mixed consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
The establishment was registered as RE-NSW-2020-0033 from 16 March 2020. The registration period lapsed on 30 June 2024 and a renewal application has not yet been lodged. Export activities have continued on the basis of the previous registration certificate.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Frances McMahon is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2014. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 33 on Plan DP 283740, located at 21 Gwydir Highway, Moree NSW 2400. The total registered area is 38.0 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for South Korea:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required with specific declarations per MAFRA guidance
Treatment Records | Full fumigation records required; NPQS may request copies
Residue MRLs | Comply with Korea MFDS MRL standards for each commodity
12. Supporting Documents
Farm Site Plan (Appendix A)
HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Horsham Wimmera Grain Co Pty Ltd
Address: 84 Station Road, Northern Territory
Commodity: White Sorghum, Hard Wheat
Scope: Receival, blending, storage, cleaning and bulk loading of food-grade sorghum and wheat at Lucinda port terminal for export. Registered area RE-QLD-1547.
Intended use: White sorghum for food processing (tortillas, beer). Wheat for milling. Destinations: Mexico, Indonesia. Retail-facing end products.
2. HACCP Team
Manager 84 (Quality Lead)
Operator 84A
Operator 84B
3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Receival / intake weighing | Bulk grain from farm trucks | Grain tipped into receival pit; moisture, protein, screenings tested
2 | Pre-cleaning | Received grain | Pre-cleaned through scalper to remove trash
3 | Drying (if required) | Wet grain (sorghum >12.5%, wheat >13%) | Dried grain to spec
4 | Storage | Dry grain | Grain allocated to export silos (S1–S8) by grade
5 | Blending | Multiple silo stocks | Blended consignment to customer specification
6 | Final cleaning / screening | Blended grain | Cleaned through gravity cleaner and de-stoner
7 | Fumigation | Cleaned grain in hold silo | Fumigated grain; treated certificate issued
8 | Sampling | Fumigated grain | Composite probe sample; NATA analysis
9 | Vessel loading | Cleared grain | Grain conveyed to bulk vessel through covered gallery
4. Hazard Analysis
Step(s) | Hazard Type | Hazard Description | Prob | Sev | Risk | CCP? | Control Summary
1 | Chem | Mycotoxin (Fumonisins, AFB1) in sorghum at receival | 3 | 3 | 9 | CCP-1 | See HACCP Control Chart
1 | Chem | Pesticide MRL exceedance | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-2 | See HACCP Control Chart
1–3 | Bio | Ergot in wheat at intake | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-3 | See HACCP Control Chart
4 | Bio | Rodent infestation in terminal silos | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-4 | See HACCP Control Chart
4 | Bio | Insect infestation (weevils, grain moths) | 2 | 2 | 4 | — | GMP / PRP control
5 | Chem | Grade/variety substitution — blending error | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-5 | See HACCP Control Chart
7 | Chem | Phosphine fumigant residue | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-6 | See HACCP Control Chart
9 | Phys | Vessel cargo hold contamination (previous cargo) | 2 | 3 | 6 | CCP-7 | See HACCP Control Chart
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival | Mycotoxin (Fumonisins/AFB1) | Intake mycotoxin rapid test; lab confirmation | Fumonisins ≤2,000 µg/kg (EU); AFB1 ≤2 µg/kg | Rapid test on each receival lot (RidaQuick strip); NATA lab confirmation on flag | Each lot at intake | Reject lot; quarantine; notify grower; DAFF notification | Quality Coordinator
CCP-2 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review; residue testing on flagged lots | MRL per Mexico / Indonesia (Codex defaults) | Spray records checked per grower; residue test 5% of lots | Per grower/season | Quarantine; reject; notify grower | Quality Coordinator
CCP-3 | Receival/Storage | Ergot in wheat | Sieve test at intake; visual inspection | <0.05% ergot bodies by weight | Sieve test + visual each wheat lot at intake | Each wheat receival lot | Reject lot; return to grower; document | Terminal Manager
CCP-4 | Storage | Rodent infestation | Bait stations — 12 stations inside terminal building | No evidence of live rodents or fresh activity | Bait stations checked but NO formal monitoring schedule or corrective action procedure documented.
⚠ DEFICIENCY: Pest monitoring frequency not specified; no corrective action procedure if infestation detected.
ACTION: Document monitoring schedule (e.g., fortnightly inspection) and corrective action steps. | Monthly (target — not documented) | NOT SPECIFIED — corrective action procedure absent | Terminal Manager
CCP-5 | Blending | Grade substitution | Automated blending system with silo ID cross-check | Blend recipe must match customer spec; tolerance ±0.5% | Blending computer log reviewed per vessel; print retained | Per vessel loading | Halt blending; investigate; re-blend; notify customer | Terminal Manager
CCP-6 | Fumigation | Phosphine residue | Licensed fumigator; ventilation protocol | ≤0.01 mg/kg residue at load-out | Fumigation certificate per event; vent period checklist | Each fumigation | Extend vent period; re-test | Quality Coordinator
CCP-7 | Vessel Loading | Vessel cargo hold contamination | Vessel hold inspection before loading; DAFF approval | Hold clean; free from previous cargo; no moisture | Hold inspection by DAFF-authorised surveyor | Per vessel | Reject loading; re-clean hold; re-inspect | Terminal Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (NQGT-HSP-001):
• Terminal cleaning: receival pit cleaned weekly; conveyor gallery swept daily; elevator boots washed monthly.
• Between commodities: blow-down of all conveyors and elevator legs before changing grain type.
• Vessel loading spout cleaned after each vessel loading.
• Personnel: safety footwear and dust masks required in operational areas; handwash on entry.
• Records: Cleaning Register (NQGT-CLN-01).
Waste Management Procedure (NQGT-WMP-001):
• Screenings: scalper waste in sealed skip; removed by contractor to composting monthly.
• Grain dust: cyclone collector emptied weekly; removed to composting.
• Vessel hold washings: water + grain residues pumped to shore reception; disposed per port environmental regulations.
• Chemical waste: fumigant sachets disposed per APVMA requirements.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (NQGT-PCP-001):
• 12 internal bait stations (Bromadiolone) in terminal building.
• Insect pitfall traps in 4 export silos.
• Phosphine fumigation available on request.
⚠ DEFICIENCY: No monitoring schedule specifying inspection frequency. No corrective action procedure if rodent activity or insect infestation is detected. Pest effectiveness CANNOT be demonstrated without documented monitoring records and corrective actions. See CCP-4 above.
ACTION: Add monitoring schedule (fortnightly inspections) and corrective action procedure.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENSWED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Horsham Wimmera Grain Co Pty Ltd. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENSWED]
No formal failed goods procedure for Horsham Wimmera Grain Co Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENSWED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Horsham Wimmera Grain Co Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).

1.  OVERVIEW
Gwydir Valley Grain is a registered export establishment located at 21 Gwydir Highway, Moree NSW 2400, NSW. The establishment holds RE Number RE-NSW-2020-0033 and is registered to handle and export Field Peas under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
WB | Weighbridge | 40 t pit type | Concrete pit, steel deck | North entry
GS | Grading Shed | 28×20 m | Steel portal, concrete floor | Centre of site
S1–S4 | Storage Bins ×4 (1,000 t ea) | Dia. 10 m | Steel on concrete | South cluster
AM | Amenities Block | 7×5 m | Brick | Adjacent GS entry
CH | Chemical Store | 5×3 m | Steel, bunded | Remote — NW corner
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 5×4 m | Enclosed room in GS | GS north end
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Pulse grader (aspiration screen) | 1 unit | Cleaning and grading
Destoner | 1 unit | Foreign material removal
Colour sorter | 1 unit | Quality grading
Bagging machine (25 kg bags) | 1 unit | Bulk export bagging
Weighbridge system | 40 t rated | Truck weighing
In-line sampler | 1 unit | Representative lot sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERNSWES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Field Peas.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 450 lux processing, 360 lux storage, 342 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Internal wall surfaces are glazed ceramic tiles (150×150 mm) from when the facility was a dairy shed in the 2010s. Approximately 15% of tiles are cracked or have open grout joints that have absorbed product residue and oils. Epoxy grout repairs have been attempted but the surface is uneven and not fully cleanable. Floor is original quarry tile — deeply pitted with accumulated product.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (1500 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1201 Rev 3): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Pulse screenings and tailings | Collection bins under aspirator — sealed | Daily removal
Dust and chaff | Bag filter on aspiration system | Weekly bag disposal
Washdown water | Floor drains → sediment sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste (bags, strapping) | Skip in external waste bay | Fortnightly collection
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated field peas residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).
8.  SERNSWES

Sewerage | Septic system — licensed — serves amenities block
Stormwater | Sheet flow to soakage trench with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 60 kVA generator — auto-start on grid failure

2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Gwydir Valley Grain used in pulse cleaning, storage and packing operations for export Chickpeas. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Chickpeas during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Henry Fenn | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Hopper | After each intake | Remove pulse residue from hopper, conveyor, and floor. Blow out crevices with compressed air. | Dry / compressed air | Receival Staff | Intake checklist
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter | After each run | Remove screenings. Brush screens and rollers. Inspect for blockages. | Dry method | Plant Operator | Run log
Storage Silos / Bins | Between lots | Full sweep-out of walls, cone, and floor. Inspect for residue and insect activity. | Dry sweep | Storage Manager | Pre-loading checklist
Packing Line / Bagging Machine | End of each shift | Clear product residue. Wipe conveyor, scales, and packing tables. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Operator | Shift log
Palletising Area / Loading Dock | After each dispatch | Remove packaging debris. Sweep dock floor. Check for spills. | Dry sweep + spot clean | Dispatch Staff | Dispatch record
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, floors, basins, toilets. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Hopper
After each intake run: Lock out receiving conveyor. Use compressed air lance to dislodge pulse residue from hopper walls, conveyor trough, and all transition points. Vacuum accumulated screenings and fine material. Inspect underside of conveyor belt for product trapping. Record in Intake Checklist.
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter
After each cleaning run: Remove accumulated screenings from collection trays and hoppers. Brush aspirator screens with dedicated brush to remove lodged seeds. For colour sorter: follow manufacturer's lens cleaning protocol. Vacuum sensor housings. Inspect all filters and replace if blocked. Record in Plant Operator Run Log.
Storage Silos / Bins
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Storage Silos / Bins in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Packing Line / Bagging Machine
End of each shift: Clear all pulse product from the line. Vacuum or brush conveyor belts, weigh hoppers, and bag former guides to remove pulse fines. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe external surfaces of bagging machine and packing bench. Check sealing jaws and heat elements for residue. Record in Shift Log.
Palletising Area / Loading Dock
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Palletising Area / Loading Dock in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Dead-stock accumulation occurs in aspirator collection trays, conveyor trough joints, and under the bagging machine floor plate. These areas are vacuumed or blown out at each run change to prevent insect harbourage.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | Floors, packing area | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Amenities, hand-contact surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
AcidRinse 500 Descaler | AgriChem Aust | Acidic cleaner | 1:50 in water | Scale mineral deposits | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Each area supervisor completes a sign-off on the shift cleaning record, confirming that cleaning has been carried out to the required standard. The site manager reviews all records at the end of each production day.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
At the last condition review (10 March 2025), persistent organic staining was observed on the floor channels and wall cladding of the grain receival area. The staining pattern is consistent with repeat wet-dry cycles. Additional chemical treatment has been trialled but full remediation has not yet been achieved.

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for malting barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Malting Barley receival | Intake of bulk and bagged malting barley from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of malting barley to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of malting barley in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-TAS-2021-0006 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 8 August 2021 and the current registration period extends to 7 August 2024. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Adam Pitt is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2017. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 10 on Plan DP 258621, located at 45 Huon Highway, Huonville TAS 7109. The total registered area is 14.0 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: malting barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of malting barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 1,200 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for United Kingdom:
Requirement | Details
Phytosanitary Certificate | Phytosanitary certificate issued by DAFF required for all consignments to United Kingdom
Import Permit | Valid import permit from United Kingdom competent authority must be obtained prior to shipment
Residue Compliance | Pesticide residues must comply with United Kingdom import MRL requirements
Fumigation | Post-harvest fumigation as required by importing country authority
12. Supporting Documents
Farm Site Plan (Appendix A)
HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

CCP-1 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary review per grower; NATA MRL test on flag lots | MRL per Singapore SFA / Hong Kong / UAE (strictest) | Spray records each grower each season; residue test on 10% of grower lots | Per grower per season | Quarantine lot; reject; notify grower; notify DAFF | QA Manager
CCP-2 | Receival | Fruit fly infestation | Visual inspection 100% of bins; orchard area fly trap records | Zero live fruit fly adults or larvae in consignment | Visual inspection at intake; QFF survey results from orchard | Each receival lot | Reject lot; notify DAFF; initiate cold treatment if protocol allows | QA Manager

6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
Hygiene and Sanitation Program (GVF-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of packhouse, grader, hydrocooler and cool store with food-safe sanitiser.
• During season: hydrocooler water changed each shift; grader rollers cleaned daily; packing tables sanitised between shifts.
• Personnel hygiene: handwash on entry; no jewellery; clean gloves and hairnets required in packing area.
• Cleaning Register (GVF-CLN-01) signed daily.
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Whyalla Steel & Grain Pty Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
Pest Control Program (WHY-PCP-001):
• General pest controls described.
• No formal monitoring schedule or corrective action procedure documented.
• Pest effectiveness cannot be demonstrated without records.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
Traceability System (GVF-TRACE-001):
• Grower → orchard block → bin ID → packing run → tray lot code.
• Packing run record: grower, variety, size, quantity, packing date, cool store location.
• Dispatch: carton lot code → container number → vessel → destination.
• Recall exercise: bi-annual forward/back trace.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal failed goods procedure for Whyalla Steel & Grain Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
This HACCP plan does not contain a section addressing phytosanitary security — specifically the maintenance of the phytosanitary status of packed fruit between inspection and export dispatch to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation.

Currently absent:
• No procedure to prevent re-infestation of DAFF-inspected fruit lots in cool storage.
• No documented control over access to cool stores containing cleared export fruit.
• No co-mingling prevention between cleared and non-cleared product in cold store.
• No documentation of integrity of phytosanitary certificates relative to stored lots.

ACTION REQUIRED: Add a Phytosanitary Security section to this HACCP plan covering:
(a) Segregation of DAFF-cleared fruit from non-cleared fruit in cool storage;
(b) Cool store access control after phytosanitary inspection;
(c) Labelling and identification of cleared lots;
(d) Prevention of re-infestation (fruit fly, codling moth) during cold storage;
(e) Integrity of phytosanitary certificate relative to consignment identity.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.

1.  OVERVIEW
Huon Valley Malt is a registered export establishment located at 45 Huon Highway, Huonville TAS 7109, TAS. The establishment holds RE Number RE-TAS-2021-0006 and is registered to handle and export Wheat under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
WB | Weighbridge + Control Room | 12×6 m | Steel portal, concrete pit | North entry — road access
RB | Receival Building | 30×18 m | Steel portal, smooth concrete floor | Centre-north of site
S1–S6 | Storage Silos ×6 (2,500 t ea) | Dia. 12 m | Galvanised steel on concrete ring beams | Central cluster
PL | Packing & Load-Out Shed | 28×18 m | Tilt-up concrete panels | South end of site
AM | Amenities Block | 8×5 m | Brick, self-contained | Adjacent to RB
CS | Chemical & Lubricant Store | 6×4 m | Steel, bunded slab | 15 m from PL
IB | DAFF Inspection Room | 6×5 m | Enclosed steel room | Between RB and PL
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Grain augers | ×6 | Transfer and load-out
Belt conveyors (sealed) | ×3 | Receival to storage
Continuous-flow dryer | 1 unit | Moisture conditioning
Weighbridge system | 80 t rated | Inbound/outbound verification
Grain quality analyser (NIR) | In-line | Protein, moisture, oil testing
Rotary screen cleaner | 1 unit | Pre-storage cleaning
In-line belt sampler | 1 unit | Representative lot sampling
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Wheat.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
LED panel lighting installed 2018: 550 lux (processing), 440 lux (storage), 418 lux (load-out). IP65-rated food-grade fittings. Annual lux-level verification by licensed electrician.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Toilet facilities are provided by a chemical toilet at the site entry gate, approximately 115 m from the packing shed. A single hand basin with cold water is plumbed adjacent to the toilet cabinet. No handwashing facilities are provided within or directly adjacent to the processing area.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
All product-contact and grain-contact surfaces are smooth, non-porous and cleanable: 3-coat epoxy floor system; FRP (fibreglass-reinforced panel) wall linings to 2.7 m; stainless-steel equipment internals. Conveyor and auger housings have hinged access panels. Full washdown of product-contact surfaces required between commodity lots per cleaning SOP.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Design features minimising pest entry: smooth wall surfaces; all roof-wall junctions factory-sealed; cable/pipe penetrations sealed with food-grade silicone; 6 mm mesh on all fixed ventilation louvres; self-closing personnel doors with magnetic seals; roller doors serviced annually to maintain threshold seal integrity; no open drainage channels.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Contained waste management infrastructure: liquid drains to bunded sump (4000 L) outside the processing building; solid waste in sealed wheeled bins with lids; external waste bay roofed and bunded on three sides with 300 mm concrete kerb and sealed slab. Organic waste composted in covered bay 50 m from processing. No open waste storage areas.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Establishment Waste Management Plan (EWMP v3.0, reviewed October 2025): details procedures for all waste streams — product spillage, packaging, liquid washdown, chemical containers and dust. Scheduled tasks on daily operations checklist, signed off by shift supervisor. Records retained 3 years minimum.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Grain spillage | Sealed collection bins under auger/conveyor discharge | Daily removal
Grain dust | Cyclone separator → sealed collection bags | Fortnightly bag disposal
Washdown water | Floor drains → bunded sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste | Compressor baler in waste bay | Monthly contractor collection
Chemical containers | Labelled, sealed store | Licensed waste contractor quarterly
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
The establishment is maintained in a clean and hygienic condition appropriate for export of Wheat. All product-contact surfaces are cleaned between commodity lots using the documented cleaning procedure. Non-product-contact surfaces cleaned on a 4-weekly schedule. No hygiene deficiencies at most recent inspection.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Pest condition assessment: Rodents: nil evidence in 6 months of monitoring. Grain insects: probe samples from all storage negative for live insects. Birds: no evidence of access to grain-contact areas. Last licensed fumigation: December 2024.
8.  SERVICES
Service | Details
Electrical supply | Three-phase 415 V — Ausgrid/Endeavour Energy connection at site entry
Water supply | mains + irrigation licence — 50 mm service
Telecommunications | NBN fixed line + mobile backup at administration/control room
Sewerage | Licensed trade waste — EPA approval — serves amenities block
Stormwater | Graded hardstand to retention basin with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 200 kVA diesel generator — auto-start on grid failure

2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers all areas of Huon Valley Malt used in nut processing and packing operations for export Walnuts. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Walnuts during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Jack Foley | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Receival / Intake Area | After each intake | Remove nut debris, hulls, shells. Sweep floor and conveyor. Clear pit. | Dry sweep | Receival Staff | Intake record
Huller / Cracker / Sheller | After each run | Dismantle screens and access panels. Remove residue. Wipe rollers and blades. | BioDegreaser FD (1:25) + rinse | Processing Operator | Equipment cleaning log
Grading & Sizing Equipment | After each run | Clear product from screens. Brush surfaces. Wipe down conveyor belts and rollers. | EnzymeClear (1:20) | Grading Operator | Run record
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer | After each drying cycle | Remove nut skins and debris. Clean dryer mesh or tray surfaces. | Dry method | Drying Supervisor | Drying log
Storage Bins / Holding Area | Between commodity lots | Full physical sweep of bin walls and floor. Inspect for residue and pest signs. | Dry sweep | Storage Manager | Pre-loading checklist
Packing Line / Packaging Area | End of each shift | Remove nut fragments from conveyor, scales, packing tables. Sweep floor. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Clean surfaces, basins, toilets, floors. Refill soap. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Area
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Huller / Cracker / Sheller
After each production run: Power off and lock out drive before opening. Dismantle outer access panels. Remove nut residue, shell fragments, and skin from rollers, screens, and internal surfaces using a stiff brush. Prepare BioDegreaser FD at 1:25. Apply to metal surfaces where oil residue is present. Contact time 5 minutes. Rinse with water. Allow to dry before reassembly. Record in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Grading & Sizing Equipment
After each run: Clear all nut product from grading screens and conveyor belts. Brush screens using designated nut-cleaning brush to remove embedded skins and fragments. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20 in a spray bottle. Spray conveyor belt and rollers. Wipe with clean cloth. Inspect for any remaining organic residue. Record in Run Record.
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Drying Area / Pads / Dryer in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Storage Bins / Holding Area
Between commodity lots: Inspect and clean storage bins before loading a new nut commodity. Using industrial vacuum, remove all residual nut material from bin walls, seams, and floor. Inspect for pest activity (insect frass, rodent droppings). Storage Manager signs pre-loading checklist confirming bin is clean and free of pests.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | Floors, storage areas | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Huller, cracker, sheller components | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading equipment, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Paper-based cleaning records are maintained in a ring-binder located at the site office. Completed records are filed monthly and stored for at least two years.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Cleaned (✓/✗) | Staff Initial
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
A trained quality officer conducts spot verification checks on a rotating schedule covering all areas within each working week. Verification findings are recorded in the Quality Inspection Register.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Non-conformances with cleaning requirements are recorded in the site's corrective action log. Root cause analysis is completed for any repeat event within 30 days. Completed corrective actions are verified by the manager and signed off before closure.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
Routine inspection of Huon Valley Malt completed on 27 January 2025. All areas assessed as compliant with the hygiene standards required for the export of Walnuts. Cleaning logs current and records up to date.

CP1.reason: All receival, cleaning, storage, sampling and dispatch activities fall within the registered malting barley export operations.

CP2.evidence: Track 1 sec 3 — 'no conditions, suspensions or reviews'
CP2.reason: Registration is declared active with no suspension against the operations, though the lapsed 7 Aug 2024 expiry is a lesser concern outside the scope of suspension.

CP3.reason: The registered export area (14.0 ha Lot 10 DP 258621) is delineated with site plan.

CP4.reason: Buildings, facilities, services and adjoining sites are described in detail.

CP5.reason: Layout of export-operation areas, permanent fixtures and equipment is documented on the site plan.

CP6.reason: No notifiable changes occurred and the notification obligation under Rule 4-6 is acknowledged.

CP7.reason: No alterations carried out; approval process for future alterations acknowledged.

CP8.reason: Establishment has the required buildings, equipment, facilities and services for grain export.

CP9.reason: Adequate lighting installed with annual lux verification.

CP10.evidence: Track 4 sec 4.3 — 'No handwashing facilities within or directly adjacent to the processing area'
CP10.reason: Only a single cold-water basin at a toilet 115 m away; no handwashing at the processing area fails the requirement.

CP11.reason: Smooth epoxy floors, FRP linings and stainless internals allow effective cleaning.

CP12.reason: Sealed junctions, mesh louvres, self-closing sealed doors and serviced roller-door seals minimise pest harbourage.

CP13.reason: Bunded sump, sealed lidded bins and roofed/bunded waste bay provide hygienic waste disposal design.

CP14.evidence: Track 4 building schedule 'IB DAFF Inspection Room'; Track 5 sec 7
CP14.reason: A dedicated enclosed DAFF inspection room and sampling facilities are provided.

CP15.evidence: Track 4/5 — rotary screen cleaner and aspirator
CP15.reason: Screening equipment manages the risk of large contaminants.

CP16.evidence: Track 5 sec 5 — 'cleaned by rotary screen and aspirator'
CP16.reason: Cleaning/screening removes large contaminants prior to storage.

CP17.reason: Comprehensive documented hygiene control system with master cleaning schedule and SOPs.

CP18.evidence: Track 4 sec 6 EWMP v3.0 waste management system
CP18.reason: A dedicated Establishment Waste Management Plan documents all waste streams and disposal, though the HACCP (Track 2) omits waste.

CP19.reason: The hygiene and waste control systems are documented and appropriate for grain export operations.

CP20.evidence: Track 7 — 21 mapped bait stations with weekly/twice-weekly servicing schedule and CAPA
CP20.reason: A mapped rodent bait-station system with a servicing schedule exists, satisfying the presence of a pest control system.

CP21.evidence: Track 2 sec 7 'effectiveness cannot be demonstrated'; Track 3 cover 'ad-hoc, no written SOP, risk assessment or scheduled treatment program'
CP21.reason: The pest system's effectiveness is not demonstrable — no formal SOP/risk assessment or documented monitoring/corrective-action program.

CP22.evidence: Track 3 pest log 2022-2025; Track 6 records kept 2 years
CP22.reason: At least two years of hygiene/waste/pest records are retained.

CP23.reason: Records are in English, dated and legible.

CP24.reason: All areas assessed clean and hygienic at most recent inspection with current cleaning logs.

CP25.evidence: Track 3 Establishment Condition — 'None detected'; Track 4 sec 7.2 nil evidence
CP25.reason: No pest evidence across all inspected areas; goods not likely infested.

CP26.evidence: Track 3 Bait Station Register 'Good'; Track 7 all stations 'Good'
CP26.reason: Bait stations and traps are recorded as fit for purpose and in good working order.

CP27.evidence: Track 7 sec 4 — 'Temporary overflow pesticide cartons held in open shelf area during stocktake'
CP27.reason: Pesticide stored on open shelving is improper chemical storage creating a contamination risk to prescribed goods.

CP28.evidence: Track 7 sec 4 — 'Chemical storage physically separated from export product handling and preparation areas'
CP28.reason: Chemical storage is stated to be physically separated from preparation areas.

CP29.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 1 Receival Register — property/paddock IDs
CP29.reason: Traceability from source property/paddock to receival is recorded.

CP30.reason: Internal movement and lot integrity while at the establishment is tracked.

CP31.evidence: Track 9 Sheet 4 Dispatch/Transfer Dockets — destination premises and RE No.
CP31.reason: Transfer to next premises is recorded with destination and seal details.

CP32.evidence: Track 9 (labelling, lot codes, records); Track 2 sec 8 traceability system
CP32.reason: Documented labelling and record-keeping controls maintain traceability and integrity.

CP33.evidence: Track 8 sec 2 — 'Flow chart omits one alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods'

CP34.evidence: Track 2 sec 9 'No formal failed goods procedure'; Track 9 Sheet 6 'blending rationale logged in shift note only'

CP35.evidence: Track 8 sec 1/5 — security zoning, sealed storage, pre-load inspections, separated hold/reject area

CP36.evidence: Track 8 sec 3 — 'Substitution controls rely on single-operator checks for selected late-shift dispatches'
CP36.reason: Single-operator dispatch verification is inadequate to minimise the risk of substitution.

2. Registered Export Operations
This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for chia seeds (specialty). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
Activity | Description | Scope Status
Chia Seeds receival | Intake of bulk and bagged chia seeds from registered growers | Within scope
Cleaning and grading | Processing of chia seeds to export specification | Within scope
Storage | Storage of chia seeds in registered receival and storage areas | Within scope
Sampling | Pre-export sampling for quality and phytosanitary inspection | Within scope
Dispatch | Loading and dispatch of certified consignments | Within scope
3. Registration Status
Registration RE-NT-2022-0008 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 18 June 2022 and the current registration period extends to 17 June 2025. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person
Bruce Nguyen is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2019. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise Lot 30 on Plan DP 161154, located at Lot 4 Victoria Highway, Katherine NT 0850. The total registered area is 8.7 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
Building / Structure | Description
Main receival shed | Steel frame, concrete floor, roller-door access, 1,200 t capacity
Silo complex (×4) | Corrugated steel upright silos, 500 t each, aeration fitted
Machinery shed | Steel frame, open-front, houses headers and augers
Chemical storage room | Lockable, ventilated, bunded, separate from grain storage
Office and amenities | Portable cabin — office, toilet, first aid kit
6.2 Services and Utilities
Service | Details
Electricity | Three-phase mains power, metered supply
Water | Mains connected; potable supply to amenities; tank water for dust suppression
Weighbridge | 60 t capacity, calibrated annually, NATA-endorsed
Drainage | Concrete hardstand with perimeter drain to collection sump
6.3 Adjoining Sites
The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow
A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: chia seeds is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities
The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of chia seeds. Total storage capacity is approximately 1,200 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes
No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises
No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for UAE:
Requirement | Details

13. Food Safety Program
A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping
Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

3. Process Flow Diagram
Step | Process | Input | Output
1 | Hull/shell receival | Field-harvested wet almonds | Almonds received at hulling intake

5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
CCP # | Process Step | Significant Hazard | Control Measure | Critical Limit | Monitoring Procedure | Frequency | Corrective Action | Responsibility
CCP-1 | Receival/Drying | Aflatoxin | NATA aflatoxin test each lot; moisture control during drying | AFB1 ≤2 µg/kg (EU); total aflatoxin ≤4 µg/kg (USA) | NATA test on every receival lot; moisture check before and after drying | Per lot at receival; post-drying | See: Failed goods procedure — [DEFICIENCY: No procedure documented for aflatoxin-positive lots] | Food Safety Manager
CCP-2 | Receival | Salmonella | Surface sanitation of intake equipment; equipment cleaning after each variety | Salmonella — not detected in 25 g | Environmental swab program (quarterly); process water hygiene | Quarterly swabs; per season water test | Intensify cleaning; environmental investigation; product quarantine if positive | Food Safety Manager
CCP-3 | Drying | PAH from dryer | Commercial ISDN-grade fuel; regular burner maintenance and calibration | BaP ≤2 µg/kg in dried product | Annual burner service; fuel quality certificate retained | Annual service; per season fuel batch | Stop dryer; service burner; test product before resuming | Processing Manager
CCP-4 | Metal Detection | Metal contamination | Inline metal detector: Fe ≥2.0 mm, non-Fe ≥2.5 mm | No metal above sensitivity limits | Metal detector calibrated each shift with test pieces | Each carton (inline) | Quarantine line; trace metal source; re-run compliant product | Processing Manager
CCP-5 | Packing | Allergen cross-contact | Dedicated almond-only lines; TACT allergen cleaning between species | No detectable cashew or walnut protein (ELISA) | ELISA test after allergen cleaning; visual inspection | After each allergen cleaning event | Re-clean; re-test; hold product | Food Safety Manager
CCP-6 | Cold Storage | Temperature abuse | Continuous datalogger; automatic alarm at >6°C | ≤4°C | Datalogger reviewed daily | Continuous | Investigate; reject deteriorated product; service refrigeration | Processing Manager
CCP-7 | Receival | Pesticide MRL | Spray diary per grower; residue test on 5% of receival lots | MRL per Japan, EU, USA (strictest applicable) | Spray records each grower each season; residue test flagged lots | Per grower/season | Quarantine; reject; notify grower | Food Safety Manager
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No site-specific hygiene and sanitation program documented for Wagga Wagga Flour Mill Pty Ltd. General industry practices are referenced but no cleaning schedules, chemicals, personnel hygiene procedures or records are defined.
Waste Management Procedure (RAP-WMP-001):
• Hulls: collected and sold to stock feed market; removed within 24 hours.
• Shells: sold to garden mulch supplier; stored in sealed covered skip.
• Sorting rejects (mouldy kernels): collected in sealed bins; sent to landfill as food waste.
• Dryer exhaust: ducted to external atmosphere away from product intakes.
• Wastewater: directed to trade waste system under council approval.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal pest control program is documented for Wagga Wagga Flour Mill Pty Ltd. No bait station map, monitoring schedule, contractor engagement or corrective action procedures are included.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)
Traceability System (RAP-TRACE-001):
• Each grower's lot assigned unique batch reference; linked to orchard ID, variety, harvest date.
• Processing records: batch reference flows through hulling, shelling, drying, sorting and packing.
• Packing lot code on each retail unit and carton.
• Dispatch: carton lot code → transport → destination.
• Recall exercise: annual forward/back trace in <4 hours.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
This HACCP plan does not include a formal procedure for managing goods that fail inspection, including blending, rejection, treatment and re-presentation of failed products.

Specifically absent:
• No written procedure for what happens when a lot tests positive for aflatoxin (CCP-1).
• No documented process for re-presenting rejected lots after corrective action.
• No record-keeping requirement for non-conforming lot disposition.

ACTION REQUIRED: Implement a Failed Goods Management Procedure covering:
(a) Immediate segregation and quarantine of suspect/failed lots;
(b) Prohibition on blending failed lots with passing lots to achieve compliance;
(c) Re-inspection / re-testing protocol;
(d) Acceptable dispositions (destruction, downgrade, return to grower);
(e) DAFF notification requirements;
(f) Records to retain (NCR form, lot disposition log, minimum 2 years).
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)
[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Wagga Wagga Flour Mill Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.

1.  OVERVIEW
Katherine Specialty Crops is a registered export establishment located at Lot 4 Victoria Highway, Katherine NT 0850, NT. The establishment holds RE Number RE-NT-2022-0008 and is registered to handle and export Almonds under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2.  BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
Code | Building / Structure | Dimensions | Construction | Location
PH | Nut Processing Hall | 32×20 m | Steel portal, smooth epoxy floor | Centre of site
HS | Hulling/Shelling Shed | 28×18 m | Steel, concrete floor | North of PH
CS | Cold Store | 14×12 m | Insulated panel, ammonia refrigeration | East of PH
AM | Amenities Block | 8×5 m | Brick | Adjacent PH entry
CH | Chemical Store | 5×3 m | Steel, bunded | SE corner
3.  EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
Item | Quantity / Spec | Purpose
Hulling and shelling line | 1 unit | Primary processing
Optical colour sorter | 1 unit | Quality grading
Semi-automatic pack line | 2 lanes | Consumer and bulk packing
Pallet stretch wrapper | 1 unit | Export palletising
4.  FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)
The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Almonds.
4.2  Lighting (C2)
T5 LED fluorescent panels on 600 mm spacing — 500 lux at floor level throughout processing area. Task lighting above grading line at 550 lux. Loading dock: 300 W LED floods at 380 lux. Emergency lighting on dedicated UPS circuit.
4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)
Self-contained amenities unit: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin — hot/cold water, liquid soap dispensers, paper towels, hand sanitiser. Sited at main processing entry (<15 m from packing line). Additional wash station at grading line head-of-line position.
5.  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1  Cleanability (C4)
Floors: smooth-trowelled reinforced concrete with penetrating sealant (applied 2008, resealed 2013); coved floor-wall junctions throughout. Wall cladding: 1.6 mm Zincalume on galvanised rails to 3.0 m — smooth, washable. All service penetrations sealed with flexible polyurethane. Drain covers: lift-out stainless-steel.
5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)
Pest exclusion features: (1) all gaps >6 mm in the building envelope sealed; (2) ventilation openings screened with 6 mm galvanised mesh; (3) all doors have rubber or brush seals at threshold and jambs; (4) drainage openings covered with SS mesh inserts; (5) no internal ledges >50 mm depth without ≥45° slope; (6) equipment on feet to eliminate floor-level harbourage. Inspected by licensed technician every 6 months.
5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6)
Waste infrastructure: (1) floor drains to grease interceptor → licensed trade waste; (2) solid product waste in sealed 240 L bins at processing line discharge — removed to covered bunded external skip, collected by contractor twice weekly; (3) packaging waste in baler at external waste bay; (4) dust and fines via bag filter — bags sealed and removed weekly. All collection points have contained, cleanable surfaces.
6.  WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7)
Waste Control System (Doc WCS-001): defines (a) waste stream classification, (b) daily/weekly/post-production cleaning tasks, (c) responsible personnel, (d) waste contractor schedule, (e) emergency spill response. Compliance records in digital operations log. Internal audit quarterly.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
Waste Type | Handling Method | Removal Frequency
Hull and shell waste | Collection pit under processor → covered external stockpile | Daily bobcat removal
Nut dust and fines | Bag filter on processing line | Weekly bag change
Washdown water | Floor drains → sump | Weekly pump-out
Packaging waste | Baler/compactor | Fortnightly collection
7.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)
Establishment condition — most recent internal inspection: processing hall floor clean, drains clear; grading equipment wiped down post-use, no residue on contact surfaces; wall linings free from dust and condensation staining; chemical store tidy with labelled containers; waste bins emptied and clean. Condition consistent with good hygiene practices.
7.2  Pest Condition (C9)
Establishment pest-free: no rodent activity (no droppings, gnaw marks or runs observed); insect pheromone traps — current catches below threshold (3 moths/week vs 10 moths/week threshold); grain probe sampling negative for live insects; bird deterrents in place and effective; all bait stations serviceable.

Stormwater | Sheet flow to soakage trench with licensed discharge point
Power backup | 60 kVA generator — auto-start on grid failure
