2.  SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers the main processing, grading, packing, and storage areas. Receival and intake dock procedures are managed under the site's Transport and Logistics Plan.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Mixed Berries during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3.  PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Role | Responsibility | Cleaning Areas
Tina Graham | Establish and review hygiene plan; approve deviations; review records | All areas
Operations Supervisor | Assign cleaning duties; verify completion; sign cleaning records | Production areas
Maintenance Officer | Clean and inspect all mechanical equipment; maintain cleaning equipment | Equipment / machinery
All Production Staff | Complete assigned daily cleaning tasks; report deficiencies to supervisor | Assigned areas
Contractor Staff | Follow hygiene plan requirements; report to site supervisor | Areas of work
4.  MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
Area / Equipment | Frequency | Cleaning Method | Chemical | Responsible | Verification
Grading & Sorting Line | After each run / Daily | Remove product residue from conveyor belts, rollers, brushes. Wipe down all surfaces. | EnzymeClear Organic Remover (1:20) | Line Supervisor | Grading log
Packing Area / Line | End of each shift | Clear line of product. Sweep floor. Clean packing tables and equipment surfaces. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Packing Supervisor | Shift cleaning record
Cold Storage / Coolrooms | Monthly / Between loads | Defrost and clean evaporator coils. Wipe walls, shelves, floor. Check drain. | AcidRinse 500 (1:50) + QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Cold Store Manager | Cold store maintenance log
Pre-Cool Chamber | Weekly | Wipe walls and shelving. Check air circulation unit and drain for organic buildup. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | Operations Staff | Weekly inspection log
Loading Dock / Dispatch | After each dispatch run | Remove packaging waste. Sweep dock floor. Check refrigerated transport door seal. | Dry sweep + spot clean | Dispatch Supervisor | Dispatch checklist
Floor Drains (all areas) | Weekly | Remove covers. Flush with hot water and cleaning agent. Scrub drain channels. | ProClean 200 (1:50) | Maintenance | Drain cleaning log
Amenities / Toilets / Lunchroom | Daily | Mop floors. Clean basins and toilets. Wipe all surfaces. | QuatSan 100 (1:100) | All staff / rostered | Supervisor check
5.  AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay
After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line
After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line
End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms
Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber
Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6.  MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES
Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7.  APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
Product Name | Manufacturer | Type | Dilution | Application | SDS Location
ProClean 200 Alkaline Detergent | AgriChem Aust | Alkaline detergent | 1:50 in water | General floors, dock surfaces | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
EnzymeClear Organic Remover | FoodSafe Solutions | Enzyme cleaner | 1:20 in water | Grading line, conveyor belts | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
QuatSan 100 Surface Sanitiser | SaniPro Pty Ltd | QAC sanitiser | 1:100 in water | Packing tables, amenities | SDS Folder — Cabinet A

BioDegreaser FD Food-Grade | CleanTech Aust | Food-grade degreaser | 1:25 in water | Machinery, conveyor chain | SDS Folder — Cabinet A
8.  RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1  Record System
Paper-based cleaning records are maintained in a ring-binder located at the site office. Completed records are filed monthly and stored for at least two years.
8.2  Sanitation Verification Log Template
Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments
9.  VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Each area supervisor completes a sign-off on the shift cleaning record, confirming that cleaning has been carried out to the required standard. The site manager reviews all records at the end of each production day.
10.  NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
If a cleaning check reveals an area is not compliant with this plan, the area is isolated and re-cleaned. The supervisor completes a Corrective Action Report within 24 hours. The report is reviewed by management and used to update training or procedures where required.
11.  ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)
The establishment was inspected by the Establishment Manager on 31 January 2025. All production areas, storage facilities, and amenities were confirmed clean and free of product residue, pest activity, and hygiene deficiencies.

cps.text: The establishment is operating within its registered operations and, where applicable, its registered functions to prepare plants or plant products for export.
At the time the export operations are carried out, the registration of the establishment must not be suspended in relation to those operations or functions.
the area of the premises that is registered for export operations
all important features of the registered area and adjoining sites, including the buildings, facilities and services to conduct the export operations
the layout of the areas where export operations occur, including all permanent fixtures, and layout of equipment used to prepare plants and plant products

Where required, notification has been provided to the department of relevant changes to the registration, including the business structure, persons in management and control, trading name, address and contact details.

Where required, notices of alterations, extensions and rearrangements to the registered establishment that may affect compliance with the conditions of registration have been submitted to and approved by the department.
The establishment has the buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the type of export operations being conducted.
There is adequate lighting for the export operations being conducted.
There is hand washing and toilet facilities at the establishment.

cps.subelement: 2.2 Design and construction of the establishment

cps.subelement: 2.2 Design and construction of the establishment
cps.text: The establishment is designed, constructed and maintained to minimise the contamination, infestation and pest harbourage during export operations.

cps.subelement: 2.2 Design and construction of the establishment
cps.text: The establishment is designed, constructed and maintained to provide the disposal of all waste material, including solids and liquids, in an efficient and hygienic manner.

The inspection areas, equipment and facilities are designed, constructed and maintained to allow for the collection, inspection and analysis of samples by an Authorised Officer for the type of prescribed plant or plant products. This includes, but is not limited to: inspection bench, where applicable.
manage the risk of contamination by large contaminants
ensure that any large contaminants are removed from the plants or plant products

The system of controls is effective for the type of export operations and activities conducted at the establishment.

contaminate prescribed plant or plant products
contaminate areas where prescribed plant or plant products are prepared

At least 2 years of traceability records are retained; including but not limited to receival, product movement, treatment, transfer records, dispatch, and transport unit approval records, where applicable.

At least 2 years of records for prescribed goods that have been rejected and/or failed export inspection are retained; including but not limited to records of blending, treatments and re-presentation of goods.
Records must: be in English; include the date of action; be accurate, legible and able to be audited.
